altitude_deficit_4000ft.plain_summary: The visiting team's home stadium normally sits at least 4,000 feet lower in elevation than the stadium they're playing in today, the kind of jump a sea-level team makes flying into Denver or Mexico City. Bet on the home team.

altitude_deficit_4000ft_division.plain_summary: The visiting team is making at least a 4,000-foot elevation jump into today's stadium, but only counting games against a division rival they make this same trip against repeatedly. The limited data so far actually leaned toward the visiting team, not the home team.

altitude_deficit_4000ft_era_2009_2017.plain_summary: The visiting team is making at least a 4,000-foot elevation jump into today's stadium, checked only in the 2009 through 2017 seasons. The limited data from that era leaned slightly away from the home team getting any benefit.

altitude_deficit_4000ft_era_2018_2025.plain_summary: The visiting team is making at least a 4,000-foot elevation jump into today's stadium, checked only in the 2018 through 2025 seasons. The limited data from that more recent era leaned toward the home team covering.

attention_battery_attention_gap_dog.plain_summary: The underdog has been generating noticeably more Wikipedia search interest than the favorite in the week before the game. This was tested as a bet on the favorite, one of six similar online-buzz comparisons tried together as a batch, and the limited data leaned away from the idea.

attention_battery_attention_gap_favorite.plain_summary: The favorite has been generating noticeably more Wikipedia search interest than the underdog in the week before the game. This was tested as a bet against that overhyped favorite, one of six similar online-buzz comparisons tried together as a batch, and the limited data leaned strongly the other way, toward the favorite covering more, not less.

attention_battery_away_hot.plain_summary: The visiting team has been generating unusually heavy Wikipedia search interest in the week before the game. This was tested as a bet on the home team, one of six similar online-buzz comparisons tried together as a batch, and the limited data leaned toward the idea.

attention_battery_both_cold.plain_summary: Both teams have been generating unusually little Wikipedia search interest in the week before the game, a sign of a low-profile matchup. This was tested as a bet on the home team, one of six similar online-buzz comparisons tried together as a batch, and the limited data leaned toward the idea. This measure of a quiet matchup is different from an earlier check that counted sportsbook listings instead of search interest.

attention_battery_both_cold_gdelt_replic.plain_summary: Both teams have been getting unusually little sports-news coverage in the week before the game, measured with a completely different online-attention source than Wikipedia: a global news-monitoring feed counting articles about each team on major sports sites. This was tested as a bet on the home team, as an independent double-check of an earlier Wikipedia-based low-attention finding, and the limited data leaned away from the idea, even though the two attention-measuring methods were shown to track each other reasonably well.

attention_battery_hot_after_loss.plain_summary: The home team has been generating unusually heavy Wikipedia search interest in the week before the game, right after losing its previous game -- a spot where the betting market might overreact to bad recent news. This was tested as a bet on that home team, one of six similar online-buzz comparisons tried together as a batch, and the limited data came back close to a coin flip.

attention_battery_hot_team_fade.plain_summary: The home team has been generating unusually heavy Wikipedia search interest in the week before the game. This was tested as a bet against that overhyped home team, one of six similar online-buzz comparisons tried together as a batch, and the limited data leaned away from the idea.

attention_followup_both_cold_non_primeti.plain_summary: Both teams have been getting unusually little Wikipedia search interest before the game, and the game itself is not in a marquee time slot (not Thursday, Saturday, Monday, or a late Sunday night kickoff). This follow-up bet on the home team, one of four checks built to dig deeper into an earlier low-attention finding, and the limited data leaned toward the idea being even stronger outside marquee time slots.

attention_followup_both_cold_small_marke.plain_summary: Both teams have been getting unusually little Wikipedia search interest before the game, and on top of that both come from smaller media markets with below-average search traffic even in a typical week. This follow-up bet on the home team, one of four checks built to dig deeper into an earlier low-attention finding, and the limited data leaned away from the idea being any stronger specifically because of market size.

attention_followup_cold_visitor_only.plain_summary: Only the visiting team has been getting unusually little Wikipedia search interest before the game; the home team's attention level is not restricted at all. This follow-up bet on the home team, one of four checks built to dig deeper into an earlier low-attention finding, and the limited data leaned toward the idea, suggesting a quiet visiting team alone may drive most of the effect.

attention_followup_deep_cold_tilt.plain_summary: Instead of using a fixed cutoff for what counts as 'a quiet game,' this checks whether the home team's covering rate rises smoothly as both teams' combined Wikipedia search interest drops, across the full range of games rather than just the quietest ones. It's one of four checks built to dig deeper into an earlier low-attention finding, and the limited data leaned toward the idea holding up as a smooth trend, not only at the extremes.

best_pick_calibrated_probability_top1.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game: this tests one way of choosing which single game to feature as the week's marquee 'Best Pick,' by ranking games according to the model's own calibrated confidence that its chosen side covers, against simply picking that featured game at random from the week's slate. It measures accuracy on a small, self-selected sample of 51 chosen picks rather than the whole week's card, and the limited data leaned against this ranking method.

best_pick_followup_alpha2000_distance.plain_summary: College football: this tests one way of choosing the week's marquee 'Best Pick' game -- ranking games by how far a differently-tuned version of the model's confidence sits from a coin flip -- against the rule actually used in production. It's a free trial run on college football data that does not use up any of the project's limited NFL test data, and the limited data leaned against switching.

best_pick_followup_dispersion_gated_smoo.plain_summary: College football: this tests a composite rule for choosing the week's marquee 'Best Pick' game -- using a different confidence-ranking method only in weeks where the model's own predictions agree unusually closely with each other, and falling back to the production rule otherwise -- against the rule actually used in production. It's a free trial run on college football data that does not use up any of the project's limited NFL test data, and the limited data leaned against switching.

best_pick_followup_ensemble_distance.plain_summary: College football: this tests choosing the week's marquee 'Best Pick' game by averaging two different confidence-ranking methods together, against the rule actually used in production. It's a free trial run on college football data that does not use up any of the project's limited NFL test data, and the limited data leaned slightly toward switching, though not by enough to clear the bar this project sets before adopting a change.

best_pick_followup_smooth_cdf_distance.plain_summary: College football: this tests choosing the week's marquee 'Best Pick' game using a specific, already-adopted change to how the model smooths its probabilities, ranked by how far that confidence sits from a coin flip, against the rule actually used in production. It's a free trial run on college football data that does not use up any of the project's limited NFL test data, and the limited data leaned toward switching, though not by enough to clear the bar this project sets before adopting a change.

best_pick_key_number_distance_top1.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game: this tests choosing the week's marquee 'Best Pick' game by how far the point spread sits from the common final-margin numbers of 3 or 7 points, against simply picking that featured game at random from the week's slate. It measures accuracy on a small, self-selected sample of 51 chosen picks rather than the whole week's card, and the limited data leaned against this ranking method.

best_pick_opener_ranker_candidate_prob_d.plain_summary: This compares two ways of choosing the week's marquee 'Best Pick' game: an unfiltered version that ranks purely by how far the model's confidence sits from a coin flip, against the rule the project actually runs in production, which adds a filter for games where the betting markets most agree with each other. Checked across 1,537 games and 107 weeks that had already been reused for related checks earlier in the same project session, so the result carries less weight than a fresh sample would; the limited data leaned slightly against the unfiltered version.

This compares two ways of choosing the week's marquee 'Best Pick' game: ranking purely by how far the model's confidence sits from a coin flip, against the rule the project actually runs in production, which instead favors the game where the model's prediction differs most from a simple baseline. Checked on a stretch of 1,537 games and 107 weeks already reused for a related check earlier in the same session, so the result carries less weight than a fresh sample would; the limited data leaned slightly toward the confidence-based version, but not by enough to change anything.

best_pick_opener_ranker_dispersion_filte.plain_summary: This compares two very similar ways of choosing the week's marquee 'Best Pick' game, both filtering to games where the betting markets most agree with each other before ranking by the model's confidence -- one of the two is the exact rule the project runs in production. Checked across 1,537 games and 107 weeks that had already been reused for related checks earlier in the same project session, so the result carries less weight than a fresh sample would. The two rules actually picked a different game in only 2 of 103 comparable weeks, and the whole measured advantage came down to a single one of those weeks.

offseason_retention_per_metric_cfb.plain_summary: College football: this tests whether letting each individual team-strength stat carry over its own separately measured share of last season's value (found to run between 17% and 35%) beats the model's simpler across-the-board setting, which carries over 67% of every stat regardless of what a per-stat estimate would suggest. Tested and resolved: the flat 67% setting wins outright, and letting each stat use its own smaller, separately estimated number actively hurt accuracy.

weak_stack_v4_forecast_weather_opener_si.plain_summary: This tests one way of feeding pregame weather forecasts into the prediction model: adding six raw forecast numbers into the model's large regression, then picking a side only by whether the market's own weather-adjusted line and the raw forecast disagree in direction, instead of using the model's usual probability output. Tested head to head against the production approach on the same 1,537 opening-line games, this version dragged accuracy down from 52.83% to 50.90%, a resolved loss rather than an inconclusive result. A separate, narrower way of using forecast weather -- applied after picks are already made, not built into the regression -- is a different construction and remains a live idea, unaffected by this result.

weak_stack_v2_narrowed_only.plain_summary: Not a bet on a specific game situation: this tests replacing the model's learned, data-fit estimate of how much an injury hurts a team with a fixed, pre-set number instead, re-checked across the model's whole population of opening-line games rather than just the narrower slice an earlier version used. It shares roughly 30% of its games with two other injury-related checks in this registry, so it should not be added to them as independent evidence, and the limited data came back almost exactly at a coin flip.

weak_stack_v2_penalty_only.plain_summary: Not a bet on a specific game situation: this tests adding a new input to the production model -- each team's penalty rate from the previous season -- checked for the first time at the project's most rigorous opening-line grading standard. It's one of three related model-tuning checks tested together on the same games, and the limited data leaned toward the new input helping.

weak_stack_v2_stack.plain_summary: Not a bet on a specific game situation: this tests combining two model changes at once -- a fixed rather than model-fit injury-severity number, plus a new team-penalty-rate input -- inside the production model, checked at the project's most rigorous opening-line grading standard. Combining them scored worse than either change tested on its own (52.43% accuracy for the combination versus 52.83% and 52.96% for the two changes separately), meaning the two changes actively worked against each other rather than adding up.

weak_stack_v3_nfl_opener_confirmation.plain_summary: Not a bet on a specific game situation: this bundles fifteen separate situational inputs together -- things like division-rivalry revenge games, a team sandwiched between two tough opponents, letdowns or bounce-backs after a blowout, penalty rates, playing-surface switches, short-week Thursday games, and long-trip travel hangovers -- and adds all fifteen to the production model at once, tested at the project's most rigorous opening-line grading standard on 1,537 games across six seasons. As a combined bundle it leaned against helping, and a meaningful 12 to 14 percent of picks flipped compared with the current model, though each of the fifteen inputs keeps its own separate finding elsewhere in this registry and this bundled result doesn't confirm or rule out any one of them individually.

weak_stack_v4_forecast_weather_opener_pr.plain_summary: Not a bet on a specific game situation: this adds six raw pregame weather-forecast numbers (temperature, wind, and similar readings from the forecast closest to kickoff) directly into the production model, tested at the project's most rigorous opening-line grading standard on 1,537 games across six seasons. Accuracy dropped from 53.36% for the current model to 52.30% with the forecast columns added, a lean against adopting this specific way of using forecast weather.

weather_battery_dome_team_outdoors_cold.plain_summary: A team that normally plays its home games in a dome is on the road at an outdoor stadium in temperatures of 40 degrees Fahrenheit or colder -- a sudden cold-weather mismatch. This was tested as a bet on the home team, one of eight weather situations tried together as a batch, using the weather that actually occurred on gameday rather than a pregame forecast (so it shows the most this kind of information could ever be worth, not something bettable before kickoff), and the limited data leaned toward the idea.

weather_battery_extreme_cold.plain_summary: The game is outdoors in temperatures of 25 degrees Fahrenheit or colder, the classic 'cold-weather home-field advantage' idea. This was tested as a bet on the home team, one of eight weather situations tried together as a batch, using the weather that actually occurred on gameday rather than a pregame forecast (so it shows the most this kind of information could ever be worth, not something bettable before kickoff), and the limited data leaned toward the idea.

weather_battery_high_altitude_road.plain_summary: This checks whether a visiting team based in a high-altitude city shows any edge playing at Denver or a Mexico City neutral-site game, but by NFL scheduling geography no visiting team is actually based at that kind of altitude, so the flag can essentially never trigger and functions as a documented non-test rather than a real check. One of eight weather situations tried together as a batch, and the data landed almost exactly at a coin flip, as expected for a flag that rarely if ever fires.

weather_battery_high_wind_outdoor.plain_summary: The game is outdoors with wind of 15 miles per hour or higher. Unlike most checks in this weather batch, this one does not predict which side benefits -- it simply measures whether windy games look different from the rest, using the weather that actually occurred on gameday rather than a pregame forecast (so it shows the most this kind of information could ever be worth, not something bettable before kickoff). One of eight weather situations tried together as a batch, and the limited data leaned toward the home team doing better in these games, without a stated reason for why home specifically should benefit.

weather_battery_high_wind_road_favorite.plain_summary: The game is outdoors with wind of 15 miles per hour or more, and the visiting team is favored to win by the betting market -- the idea that wind disrupts a favored team's passing game on the road. This was tested as a bet on the home underdog, one of eight weather situations tried together as a batch, using the weather that actually occurred on gameday rather than a pregame forecast (so it shows the most this kind of information could ever be worth, not something bettable before kickoff), and the limited data leaned away from the idea.

weather_battery_surface_switch_grass_to_.plain_summary: The visiting team normally plays its home games on grass, but today's game is on artificial turf -- a sudden change in footing and playing speed. This was tested as a bet on the home team, one of eight weather-and-surface situations tried together as a batch, using the surface and conditions that actually applied on gameday. It is one of the stronger results in the batch, with even the low end of its measured range still favoring the home team, but because it is one of several situations mined together rather than a single planned test, it is being kept on the books as still unproven rather than treated as a confirmed rule.

weather_battery_thursday_outdoor_cold.plain_summary: The game is on a Thursday, outdoors, in temperatures of 35 degrees Fahrenheit or colder -- combining a short week for both teams with cold weather. This was tested as a bet on the home team, one of eight weather situations tried together as a batch, using the weather that actually occurred on gameday rather than a pregame forecast (so it shows the most this kind of information could ever be worth, not something bettable before kickoff), and the limited data leaned toward the idea, though the range of plausible effect sizes stayed narrow and close to zero at one end.

weather_battery_warm_team_cold_late.plain_summary: The visiting team is based in a warm-winter city, and it's week 13 or later in the season with an outdoor temperature of 35 degrees Fahrenheit or colder -- a warm-weather team facing a late-season cold snap it isn't built for. This was tested as a bet on the home team, one of eight weather situations tried together as a batch, using the weather that actually occurred on gameday rather than a pregame forecast (so it shows the most this kind of information could ever be worth, not something bettable before kickoff), and the limited data leaned toward the idea.

weather_followup_high_wind_pass_heavy_vi.plain_summary: The game is outdoors with wind of 15 miles per hour or more, and the visiting team relied heavily on passing rather than running the previous season -- the idea that a pass-first visiting offense suffers more in the wind. This follow-up bet on the home team, one of five checks built to dig deeper into an earlier wind finding, and the limited data leaned slightly away from the idea.

weather_followup_rest_disadvantage_cold.plain_summary: The visiting team has fewer rest days than the home team, and the game is outdoors in temperatures of 35 degrees Fahrenheit or colder -- pairing a short-rest travel disadvantage with cold weather. This follow-up bet on the home team, one of five checks built to dig deeper into earlier weather findings, and the limited data landed close to a coin flip, leaning only slightly toward the idea.

weather_followup_surface_switch_x_outdoo.plain_summary: The visiting team normally plays on grass, today's game is on turf, it's outdoors, and the temperature is 45 degrees Fahrenheit or colder -- combining the grass-to-turf footing change with cold weather. This follow-up bet on the home team is one of five checks built to dig deeper into an earlier grass-to-turf finding, and the limited data leaned toward the idea, in line with the larger effect the earlier, simpler version of this finding already showed.

weather_followup_temp_gap_cold_visitor.plain_summary: This measures the gap between the visiting team's typical home-game temperature for that season and today's actual temperature, requiring at least a 25-degree-colder swing outdoors -- a sliding-scale version of the 'warm team meets sudden cold' idea rather than a fixed cutoff. It's one of five checks built to dig deeper into earlier weather findings, tested as a bet on the home team, and the data leaned toward the idea, with even the low end of the measured range just barely favoring the home team.

weather_followup_wind_gap_visitor.plain_summary: This measures the gap between the visiting team's typical home-game wind for that season (8 miles per hour or calmer) and today's actual wind (15 miles per hour or higher) -- a visiting team facing much windier conditions than it's used to. It's one of five checks built to dig deeper into earlier weather findings, tested as a bet on the home team, and the limited data leaned toward the idea.

weather_oracle_ceiling_opener_probabilit.plain_summary: Not a bet, and not something anyone could ever actually have before kickoff: this control test hands the model the weather that truly occurred on gameday, as if the forecast were perfect, to measure the absolute most that better weather forecasting could ever be worth to the production model. Even perfect information made accuracy worse, not better (53.36% fell to 52.23%), which rules out 'the forecast just isn't accurate enough' as the reason an earlier weather-forecast test underperformed; for wind specifically, the same method puts the ceiling on a better wind source at only about -0.07 points, essentially nothing. This result only concerns feeding raw weather into the model's core regression -- it says nothing about a handful of separate, narrower weather-based picks elsewhere in this registry that remain live possibilities.

wxtot_cold35_top_total.plain_summary: The game is outdoors, the actual temperature is 35 degrees Fahrenheit or colder, and the market's pregame scoring total is among the highest sent out that week -- cold weather paired with a high-scoring expectation, predicted to work against the side this checked favored. The result came back essentially at zero, pointing the predicted direction but too small on its own to mean much.

wxtot_precip60_top_total.plain_summary: The pregame forecast gives at least a 60% chance of rain or snow, and the market's scoring total for the game is among the highest sent out that week -- predicted to work against the side this checked favored, similar to a related cold-weather check. Instead the measured result landed clearly on the opposite side of that prediction in both ways the data was sliced, agreeing instead with a separate finding elsewhere in this registry that a high rain-or-snow forecast favors the home team; a quirk in how directions are recorded here kept this from being auto-labeled a confirmed reversal, but the underlying data is one-sided. It overlaps closely with that related rain-forecast finding and should not be counted as separate, independent confirmation of it.

wxtot_wind15_bottom_total.plain_summary: Control check: this looks at windy outdoor games (15 miles per hour or more) where the market's scoring total is among the lowest sent out that week, a combination where no effect was expected going in, since wind is usually thought to matter most in high-scoring, pass-heavy games. Instead the data leaned positive here too, even more than in the high-total version of this same wind check, which undercuts the idea that wind's effect is really about high-scoring games specifically.

wxtot_wind15_top_total.plain_summary: The game is outdoors with wind of 15 miles per hour or more, measured at kickoff rather than forecast in advance, and the market's scoring total is among the highest sent out that week -- predicted to make the favored side less likely to cover in a high-scoring, wind-affected game. The measured result pointed the opposite way from that prediction, and this check overlaps heavily with a broader high-wind check elsewhere in this registry, so it should not be counted as separate, independent evidence.

residual_location_train_recency_hl200_cf.plain_summary: College football: this tests weighting the games used to train the model so that games from roughly the last 200 games count more than older ones, compared with the model's current approach of weighting every past game equally. It's a free trial run on college football data that doesn't use up any of the project's limited NFL test budget, and the limited data came back close to even.

residual_location_train_recency_hl400_cf.plain_summary: College football: this tests weighting the games used to train the model so that games from roughly the last 400 games count more than older ones, compared with the model's current approach of weighting every past game equally. It's a free trial run on college football data that doesn't use up any of the project's limited NFL test budget, and of several recency-weighting settings tried, this one came closest to clearing the bar the researchers set before they'd trust it, though it still didn't clear it.

residual_location_train_recency_hl800_cf.plain_summary: College football: this tests weighting the games used to train the model so that games from roughly the last 800 games count more than older ones, compared with the model's current approach of weighting every past game equally. It's a free trial run on college football data that doesn't use up any of the project's limited NFL test budget, and the limited data leaned toward the idea without confirming it.

respiratory_away_market_elevated.plain_summary: The visiting team's home state is in the worst 10% of its own history for combined COVID, flu, and RSV emergency-room visits in the days right before the game. Bet on the home team; this extends an earlier flu-only version of the same idea to cover all three respiratory illnesses together, and usable data really only covers the 2024 and 2025 seasons, because the health records needed to check this point-in-time weren't actually published until years after the fact for earlier seasons.

respiratory_differential_home_worse.plain_summary: Narrowed to games where only one team's home state, not both, is in the worst 10% of its own history for combined COVID, flu, and RSV emergency-room visits right before the game -- specifically games where it's the home team's state that's elevated and the visiting team's isn't. Bet against that home team, but this slice has very few qualifying games (50), so the result is little more than a rough read.

respiratory_home_market_elevated.plain_summary: The home team's own state is in the worst 10% of its own history for combined COVID, flu, and RSV emergency-room visits in the days right before the game. Bet against the home team, and the limited data so far came back exactly even, no lean either way.

respiratory_peak_away_elevated.plain_summary: Restricted to the handful of weeks each season already flagged in an earlier flu study as the annual illness peak: the visiting team's home state is elevated for combined COVID, flu, and RSV emergency-room visits during that peak window. Bet on the home team, and the very small number of qualifying games so far leaned slightly the other way.

respiratory_peak_home_elevated.plain_summary: Restricted to the handful of weeks each season already flagged in an earlier flu study as the annual illness peak: the home team's own state is elevated for combined COVID, flu, and RSV emergency-room visits during that peak window. Bet against the home team, and the very small number of qualifying games so far leaned slightly toward the home team instead.

ridge_alpha_2000_nfl_opener_confirmation.plain_summary: Not a bet on any game: this tests swapping one of the live model's own settings -- the dial that controls how heavily it smooths noise out of its inputs -- from its current value of 10 up to 2,000, a setting that had worked better in college football testing, then checks the swap head-to-head against the current setting on the real NFL opening-line record. The swap was tested and rejected: at the openers the project actually plays, the higher setting looked about 19-to-1 likely to be worse, not better, so the model kept its original setting.

ridge_alpha_global.plain_summary: College football: this tests turning up the same model-smoothing dial (from 10 to a wide range including 2,000-2,500) using only the free college football data. A much higher setting made the model's own confidence levels noticeably more trustworthy on that data, but did not change how many picks the model actually got right, so the finding was routed toward whichever part of the system relies on trustworthy confidence numbers (like ranking picks by how sure the model is) rather than toward the accuracy setting itself.

roof_battery_closed_benign_forecast_vs_o.plain_summary: A team plays at a stadium with a retractable roof and chooses to keep it CLOSED even though the forecast that day was mild (50F or warmer, wind under 15 mph) -- a 'didn't need to close it' situation rather than a weather-forced one. This was tested, with no direction guessed in advance, as one of five checks in a roof-decision batch, and the limited data (145 qualifying games) leaned toward the home team covering less often in that spot -- though the finding can only be used in the last-minute pregame refresh, not this project's usual Tuesday betting deadline, since the actual roof decision isn't announced until roughly 90 minutes before kickoff.

roof_battery_home_cover_open_vs_closed.plain_summary: At one of the five NFL stadiums with a retractable roof, the roof is OPEN for today's game rather than closed, stripping that team of its usual climate-controlled home-field identity. This was tested as a bet against that home team, one of five checks in a roof-decision batch, and the limited data leaned toward the idea (home teams covered less with the roof open), consistently across both an earlier and a more recent stretch of seasons -- though the finding can only be used in the last-minute pregame refresh, not this project's usual Tuesday betting deadline, since the actual roof decision isn't announced until roughly 90 minutes before kickoff.

roof_battery_home_cover_open_vs_closed_o.plain_summary: At one of the five NFL stadiums with a retractable roof, the roof is OPEN for today's game rather than closed. This bet on the home team is graded using the Tuesday opening line instead of the closing line, one of five checks in a roof-decision batch, and this version of the data leaned toward the home team actually covering more with the roof open -- though the finding can only be used in the last-minute pregame refresh, not this project's usual Tuesday betting deadline, since the actual roof decision isn't announced until roughly 90 minutes before kickoff.

roof_battery_total_covered_open_vs_close.plain_summary: This one is about the total-points (over/under) market, not which team wins against the spread, so it answers a different betting question. At one of the five NFL stadiums with a retractable roof, the roof is OPEN rather than closed, exposing the game to real outdoor wind and cold that the total-points line -- set assuming a controlled environment -- may not fully price in. This was tested as a bet on the UNDER, one of five checks in a roof-decision batch, and the limited data leaned toward the idea, more strongly in the earlier era of seasons studied than the more recent one -- though the finding can only be used in the last-minute pregame refresh, not this project's usual Tuesday betting deadline, since the actual roof decision isn't announced until roughly 90 minutes before kickoff.

roof_battery_visiting_dome_open_vs_close.plain_summary: A visiting team that only ever plays indoors at home is traveling to one of the five NFL stadiums with a retractable roof, and that roof happens to be OPEN, exposing that dome-only team to real outdoor conditions it isn't used to. This was tested as a bet against that visiting team, one of five checks in a roof-decision batch, but there are only a handful of qualifying games in the whole study (10 total), so the result is little more than a curiosity -- and the finding can only be used in the last-minute pregame refresh, not this project's usual Tuesday betting deadline, since the actual roof decision isn't announced until roughly 90 minutes before kickoff.

A visiting team that only ever plays indoors at home is traveling to one of the five NFL stadiums with a retractable roof, and that roof happens to be OPEN, graded here using the Tuesday opening line instead of the closing line. Only 3 games in the entire study even qualify, so it is recorded only for completeness and tells us essentially nothing on its own -- and in any case the finding can only be used in the last-minute pregame refresh, not this project's usual Tuesday betting deadline, since the actual roof decision isn't announced until roughly 90 minutes before kickoff.

sagarin_battery_large_divergence_close.plain_summary: A computer power-rating system (Sagarin) disagrees with the closing betting line by at least 3 points on this game. Bet with the power rating's side over the market, and the limited data, graded against the closing line, leaned slightly against the idea.

sagarin_battery_large_divergence_era_201.plain_summary: A computer power-rating system (Sagarin) disagrees with the closing betting line by at least 3 points on this game, checked only in the 2010 through 2016 seasons. Betting with the power rating's side over the market leaned toward working in this earlier era.

A computer power-rating system (Sagarin) disagrees with the closing betting line by at least 3 points on this game, checked only in the 2017 through 2025 seasons. Betting with the power rating's side over the market leaned against working in this more recent era -- the 2010-2016 slice of this same setup leaned the opposite way, toward it working, so the two eras disagree and neither settles the question.

sagarin_battery_large_divergence_open.plain_summary: A computer power-rating system (Sagarin) disagrees with the Tuesday opening betting line by at least 3 points on this game. Betting with the power rating's side over the market, using only 2020-2025 games where the opening line is on record, leaned against the idea.

sagarin_battery_model_agreement_close.plain_summary: Not a bet on any specific game situation: this checks whether the project's own prediction model gets more picks right in games where a computer power-rating system (Sagarin) happens to agree with the model's chosen side, versus games where the two disagree. The model was actually very slightly more accurate on the games where it DISAGREED with the power rating, the opposite of what you'd expect if agreement were a good sign, though the sample is too small to call this settled.

sagarin_battery_top_decile_close.plain_summary: A computer power-rating system (Sagarin) disagrees with the closing betting line by an unusually large amount -- among the biggest 10% of disagreements ever seen in this dataset. Bet with the power rating's side over the market, and the limited data leaned fairly strongly toward the idea, though the sample of games this extreme is not large.

sagarin_battery_top_decile_open.plain_summary: A computer power-rating system (Sagarin) disagrees with the Tuesday opening betting line by an unusually large amount -- among the biggest 10% of disagreements ever seen in this dataset. Betting with the power rating's side over the market, using only 2020-2025 games where the opening line is on record, leaned against the idea, and the sample of games this extreme is small.

sbr_opener_era_2011_2014.plain_summary: Not a new bet, but a re-check of the project's existing production prediction rule using a different sportsbook's opening line (SBR/Sports Book Review) as the record of 'the opener,' instead of the project's usual source, to see if the model's edge depends on whose opening line you use -- checked only in the 2011 through 2014 seasons, the earliest era with enough games to test. The limited data leaned slightly against the model's usual edge holding up in this era under this alternate opening-line source.

sbr_opener_era_2015_2019.plain_summary: Not a new bet, but a re-check of the project's existing production prediction rule using a different sportsbook's opening line (SBR/Sports Book Review) as the record of 'the opener,' instead of the project's usual source -- checked only in the 2015 through 2019 seasons. The limited data leaned toward the model's usual edge holding up in this era under this alternate opening-line source.

sbr_opener_era_2020_2021.plain_summary: Not a new bet, but a re-check of the project's existing production prediction rule using a different sportsbook's opening line (SBR/Sports Book Review) as the record of 'the opener,' instead of the project's usual source -- checked only in the 2020 and 2021 seasons, the most recent years that sportsbook's public archive covers. The limited data leaned strongly toward the model's usual edge holding up in this era under this alternate opening-line source.

sbr_opener_pooled_2011_2021.plain_summary: Not a new bet, but a re-check of the project's existing production prediction rule using a different sportsbook's opening line (SBR/Sports Book Review) as the record of 'the opener,' instead of the project's usual source, combining every season from 2011 through 2021 that sportsbook's public archive covers into one overall read. The combined data leaned toward the model's usual edge holding up under this alternate opening-line source, though individual years within that stretch varied quite a bit.

shrunk_overlay_policy_walkforward.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game, and not itself playable: this tests a machine-learning method for deciding, week to week, when to flip away from the model's usual pick, by combining seven separate override signals into one learned rule, retrained fresh after every week using only information available at the time. Tested against simply never flipping, this method actually made picks worse, not better.

special_teams_composite_edge_bottom_quar.plain_summary: A team ranked in the bottom quarter of the league last season on an overall special-teams scorecard (field goals, punting, and both kinds of returns combined). Bet against that team, and the limited data leaned toward the idea.

special_teams_composite_edge_top_quartil.plain_summary: A team ranked in the top quarter of the league last season on an overall special-teams scorecard (field goals, punting, and both kinds of returns combined), the kind of team whose special teams routinely gives it better field position than expected. Bet on that team, and the limited data leaned toward the idea.

special_teams_fg_kicker_bottom_quartile.plain_summary: A team's field-goal kicker was in the bottom quarter of the league last season at making kicks relative to how hard they were. Bet against that team, and the limited data came back almost exactly even, no real lean either way. This specific field-goal-only trait was also found to barely repeat from one season to the next for the same team, which limits how much it could ever predict.

special_teams_fg_kicker_top_quartile.plain_summary: A team's field-goal kicker was in the top quarter of the league last season at making kicks relative to how hard they were. Bet on that team, and the limited data actually leaned the other way, against the idea. This specific field-goal-only trait was also found to barely repeat from one season to the next for the same team, which limits how much it could ever predict.

special_teams_punt_net_bottom_quartile.plain_summary: A team's punter was in the bottom quarter of the league last season on net punting yards (after accounting for returns). Bet against that team, and the limited data leaned toward the idea.

special_teams_punt_net_top_quartile.plain_summary: A team's punter was in the top quarter of the league last season on net punting yards (after accounting for returns). Bet on that team, and the limited data leaned the other way, against the idea.

special_teams_return_bottom_quartile.plain_summary: A team was in the bottom quarter of the league last season at both punt and kickoff returns combined. Bet against that team, and the limited data leaned toward the idea.

special_teams_return_top_quartile.plain_summary: A team was in the top quarter of the league last season at both punt and kickoff returns combined. Bet on that team, and the limited data leaned strongly toward the idea, the strongest lean of the four special-teams traits tested this way.

surface_familiarity_r1_turf_venue_visito.plain_summary: A game is being played on artificial turf, and the visiting team normally plays its own home games on grass, so it is unfamiliar with the surface underfoot -- compared with a visiting team that is turf-accustomed playing at the exact same kind of venue. Bet against that grass-accustomed visiting team, a deliberately narrower, cleaner re-test of an earlier finding that had mixed up 'plays on turf' with 'visitor unused to turf,' and the narrower version came back even stronger than the original, more so in recent seasons (2018 onward) than in the earlier stretch studied.

surface_familiarity_r2_grass_venue_mirro.plain_summary: A game is being played on natural grass, and the visiting team normally plays its own home games on turf, so it is unfamiliar with the surface underfoot -- the mirror-image check of the same idea tested on turf venues, done to see whether being unused to the surface hurts a visitor in both directions equally. It doesn't: this grass-side version came back close to a coin flip and even leaned slightly the wrong way, which argues against a simple two-way 'any surface change hurts' mechanism and suggests something specific to turf venues instead.

surface_familiarity_r3_era_2009_2017.plain_summary: A game is being played on artificial turf, and the visiting team normally plays its own home games on grass, so it is unfamiliar with the surface underfoot -- checked only in the 2009 through 2017 seasons. Betting against that grass-accustomed visiting team leaned toward working in this era, though only mildly.

surface_familiarity_r3_era_2018_2025.plain_summary: A game is being played on artificial turf, and the visiting team normally plays its own home games on grass, so it is unfamiliar with the surface underfoot -- checked only in the 2018 through 2025 seasons. Betting against that grass-accustomed visiting team leaned strongly toward working in this more recent era, though because this era overlaps the exact seasons the underlying idea was first discovered in, this strong reading is treated as reinforcing the earlier finding rather than as fresh, independent proof.

surface_profile_opener_head_to_head.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game: this compares two versions of the prediction model head-to-head using the Tuesday opening line -- the production model as-is, against a version that adds one extra input flagging exactly the grass-team-visiting-turf situation directly into the model's own math. Adding that input made the model slightly less accurate at the opener in this test, though a mirror test using the closing line instead leaned the other way, so the two grading standards disagree and neither settles it; either way, this input is not adopted in production, partly because a separate, already-live rule already applies a similar adjustment after the model's picks are made, and running both at once would double up the same idea.

surface_switch_feature_arm.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game: this tests adding one extra input to the prediction model -- flagging games where the visiting team normally plays on grass but today's game is on turf -- directly into the model's own math, then checks whether that changes how many picks the model gets right using the closing line to grade. The limited data leaned toward it helping a little, but not by enough to be confident, and it is not adopted in production.

team_style_deep_ball_outdoor_wind.plain_summary: The visiting team throws unusually deep passes as a matter of style (top quarter of the league last season), and today's game is outdoors with wind of 15 mph or more, a combination where the deep passing game should struggle. Bet on the home team, and the limited data -- based on the actual wind measured at kickoff, not a forecast, so this is closer to a best-case ceiling than something usable ahead of time -- came back almost exactly even.

team_style_distinct_identity.plain_summary: A team plays in a way that is unusually different from the league average overall, combining nine separate style traits (like pass depth, pace, and how often it lines up in shotgun) into one 'how unusual is this team's identity' score, in the top quarter of the league last season. This was tested with no direction guessed in advance, and the limited data leaned toward that team covering LESS often, though not enough to call it settled.

team_style_pace_mismatch_dog_cover.plain_summary: The home and away teams have a very different season-long pace of play (top quarter of the league in pace mismatch), the idea being that a slower, choppier game with fewer possessions gives the underdog a better chance. Bet on the underdog, and the limited data leaned toward the idea.

team_style_short_game_identity.plain_summary: A team relies unusually heavily on short passes as a matter of style (top quarter of the league last season). This was tested with no direction guessed in advance, and the limited data leaned toward that team covering MORE often.

team_style_short_game_vs_pressure_defens.plain_summary: The visiting team relies unusually heavily on short passes as a matter of style, and the home team's defense forces opponents into obvious passing situations unusually often (both in the top quarter of the league last season) -- a matchup where the home defense's pressure should disrupt the visitor's short-passing game plan. Bet on the home team, and the limited data leaned slightly the other way, against the idea.

travel_rest_away_off_bye.plain_summary: The visiting team is coming off its bye week or an unusually long rest (13 or more days), one of eight schedule-based checks tried together as a batch, all built from information available well before kickoff. Bet against the home team, and the limited data leaned against the idea, toward the home team doing about as well or better anyway.

travel_rest_eastbound_multizone.plain_summary: The team traveling to this game is crossing at least two time zones eastward from its own home base, the kind of body-clock disruption that's supposed to hurt the visiting team, one of eight schedule-based checks tried together as a batch. Bet on the home team, and the limited data leaned against the idea.

travel_rest_home_off_bye.plain_summary: The home team is coming off its bye week or an unusually long rest (13 or more days), one of eight schedule-based checks tried together as a batch. Bet on the home team, and the limited data leaned against the idea, toward the home team actually doing a bit worse.

travel_rest_international_game.plain_summary: The game is being played at a neutral or international site, so the designated 'home' team isn't actually playing at its real home stadium, one of eight schedule-based checks tried together as a batch. Bet against the home team, and the limited data came back almost exactly even.

travel_rest_long_distance_road.plain_summary: The visiting team is traveling 1,500 miles or more to get to this game, one of eight schedule-based checks tried together as a batch. Bet on the home team, and the limited data leaned against the idea.

travel_rest_return_trip_hangover.plain_summary: The home team just returned from a long trip of its own (1,500-plus miles in its previous game) and hasn't had much time to recover since (8 days or less), a possible fatigue hangover, one of eight schedule-based checks tried together as a batch. Bet against that home team, and the limited data leaned toward the idea.

travel_rest_short_week_road.plain_summary: The visiting team is playing on short rest, 5 days or less since its last game, one of eight schedule-based checks tried together as a batch, testing whether short rest costs a team more specifically when it also has to travel. Bet on the home team, and the limited data leaned mildly toward the idea.

travel_rest_thursday_pure.plain_summary: The game is simply being played on a Thursday, regardless of weather or venue, one of eight schedule-based checks tried together as a batch (kept separate from a related check that also requires cold outdoor conditions on top of the Thursday game). Bet on the home team, and the limited data leaned toward the idea.

txn_away_churn_elevated.plain_summary: The visiting team has made at least one public roster move -- a signing, release, trade, injured-reserve placement, practice-squad move, waiver claim, or suspension -- announced after this week's Wednesday roster-move cutoff and before kickoff. This was tested as a bet against that visiting team, one of several checks in a roster-transaction batch, and the limited data leaned toward the idea, more so when scored by season than by week.

txn_away_ir_placement_since_freeze.plain_summary: The visiting team placed at least one player on injured reserve after this week's Wednesday roster-move cutoff and before kickoff. This was tested as a bet against that visiting team, one of several checks in a roster-transaction batch, and the limited data leaned mildly toward the idea.

txn_away_ps_elevation_72h.plain_summary: The visiting team promoted at least one player from its practice squad in the 72 hours before kickoff. This was tested as a bet against that visiting team, one of several checks in a roster-transaction batch, but only 9 games in the whole study qualify, and the limited data that does exist actually leaned the other way, toward the visiting team doing fine.

txn_differential_home_worse_churn.plain_summary: Narrowed to games where only one side, not both, made a public post-cutoff roster move -- specifically games where it's the home team that made a move and the visiting team didn't. Bet against that home team, and the limited data came back almost exactly even.

txn_home_churn_elevated.plain_summary: The home team has made at least one public roster move -- a signing, release, trade, injured-reserve placement, practice-squad move, waiver claim, or suspension -- announced after this week's Wednesday roster-move cutoff and before kickoff. This was tested as a bet against that home team, one of several checks in a roster-transaction batch, and the limited data leaned toward the idea, more so when scored by season than by week.

txn_home_ir_placement_since_freeze.plain_summary: The home team placed at least one player on injured reserve after this week's Wednesday roster-move cutoff and before kickoff. This was tested as a bet against that home team, one of several checks in a roster-transaction batch, and the limited data leaned toward the idea, though not strongly.

txn_home_ps_elevation_72h.plain_summary: The home team promoted at least one player from its practice squad in the 72 hours before kickoff. This was tested as a bet against that home team, one of several checks in a roster-transaction batch, but only 7 games in the whole study qualify, and the limited data that does exist leaned toward the idea.

venue_milestone_home_opener.plain_summary: It's the home team's first home game of the season, the idea being that an energized season-opening home crowd gives it an edge. Bet on the home team, and the limited data leaned against the idea, toward the home team doing worse in that spot, not better.

venue_milestone_new_stadium_debut.plain_summary: A franchise is playing its very first regular-season home game ever at a brand-new stadium. This was tested as a bet against the home team (new-venue jitters), but there have only ever been 12 such games in the study period, and the tiny amount of data that exists leaned the other way, toward the home team doing fine.

venue_milestone_post_bye_home.plain_summary: It's the home team's first game back after a bye week (at least a 12-day gap). Bet on the home team, and the limited data leaned against the idea; this overlaps closely with a separate, near-identical bye-week check elsewhere in this registry, a disclosed overlap rather than an independent confirmation.

venue_milestone_post_bye_road.plain_summary: It's the visiting team's first game back after a bye week (at least a 12-day gap). Bet against that visiting team, and the limited data came back almost exactly even, with only a very slight lean against the idea that a bye week matters more for the home team than the road team.

vi_disp_homecover_top_vs_bottom_tercile.plain_summary: Multiple sportsbooks disagree with each other unusually widely about the spread on this game as of the Tuesday/Wednesday betting boards -- among the top third of most-disagreed-upon games -- compared with games in the bottom third, where the books are unusually close together. Bet on the home team, using only 2009-2016 seasons, and the limited data leaned fairly strongly toward the idea, though this is a second, related look at a family of checks built on the very same stretch of games as several other entries in this registry, so it should not be treated as independent confirmation of them.

vi_disp_movement_top_vs_bottom_tercile.plain_summary: This one measures how much the final betting line moved from open to close, in points, not whether a pick was right, so it answers a different question on a different scale than most entries here. Multiple sportsbooks disagree with each other unusually widely about the spread on this game as of the Tuesday/Wednesday boards -- the idea being that more early disagreement should mean more repricing by kickoff -- compared with games where the books agree closely. The limited 2009-2016 data leaned slightly the other way, toward less line movement in the high-disagreement games, not more, and one single early season in the data is a likely outlier skewing this read.

vi_dispersion_bottom_tercile_underdog.plain_summary: This is a deliberately unplayable control check, not a bet to make: it looks at games where multiple sportsbooks agree closely with each other on the spread (the bottom third of disagreement, i.e. a calm, 'sharp consensus' baseline) and asks whether betting the underdog in exactly those calm-market games still shows a signal. It does show a strong lean toward the underdog in the data, which matters for reading a related 'high disagreement' finding elsewhere in this registry: the two are correlated results from the same pool of games and should not be added together as if independent.

vi_dispersion_top_tercile_favorite.plain_summary: Multiple sportsbooks disagree with each other unusually widely about the spread on this game as of the Tuesday/Wednesday boards -- among the top third of most-disagreed-upon games. This was tested as a bet against the favorite (the mirror side of a related underdog check on the same games), and the limited data leaned against the idea.

vi_dispersion_top_tercile_underdog.plain_summary: Multiple sportsbooks disagree with each other unusually widely about the spread on this game as of the Tuesday/Wednesday boards -- among the top third of most-disagreed-upon games, the idea being that heavy disagreement between books means stale, unreliable pricing worth betting against. Bet on the underdog, and the limited data leaned against the idea; a related control check on the calm, low-disagreement games actually showed a stronger lean toward the underdog than this high-disagreement group did, which undercuts the original mechanism.

vi_totaldisp_overshoot_top_vs_bottom_ter.plain_summary: This one is about the total-points (over/under) market, not which team wins against the spread, and it's measured in points of overshoot past the total line, not pick accuracy, so it answers a different question on a different scale. Multiple sportsbooks disagree with each other unusually widely about the total-points line on this game as of the Tuesday/Wednesday boards -- among the top third of most-disagreed-upon games -- compared with the bottom third. Both groups of games finished under their opening total on average, and the high-disagreement group undershot by even more than the low-disagreement group, the opposite of what was expected, though the underlying idea for which direction to expect was only weakly grounded to begin with.

cfb_surface_familiarity_grass_venue_mirr.plain_summary: College football: within games played on a grass-surface field, this compares visiting teams whose own home field is artificial turf (a surface mismatch) against visiting teams who also normally play on grass, looking at whether the home team covers. It is a deliberate mirror check that is expected to show nothing if the real surface-familiarity idea is genuine, and it did come back close to a coin flip, leaning slightly against the home team.

cfb_surface_familiarity_turf_venue_visit.plain_summary: College football: within games played on an artificial-turf field, the visiting team's own home surface is normally grass (a mismatch) rather than also turf. Bet on the home team; college football's version of this idea actually showed a larger point estimate than its NFL counterpart, though on its own it isn't yet statistically conclusive.

cfb_surface_switch_grass_to_turf.plain_summary: College football: the visiting team's home field is normally grass, and today's game is on artificial turf. Bet on the home team; college football's version of this idea pointed the same direction as its NFL counterpart, but with a smaller edge.

cfb_transfer_hierarchical_accuracy_proxy.plain_summary: College football: not a bet on any single game -- this is an internal test of a modeling technique, checking whether letting the weaker Group-of-Five conference teams' ratings borrow statistical strength from the stronger Power-Five conference, rather than being estimated entirely on their own, improves the model's picking accuracy. It's a stand-in test used because a real college-to-NFL knowledge-transfer experiment hasn't been run yet; on pick accuracy specifically the limited data leaned positive without being conclusive, while a related version of the same idea judged on how well-calibrated the probabilities were (not pick accuracy) already came back clearly positive.

cfb_value_weighted_role_continuity.plain_summary: College football: tests whether valuing which players return at each roster spot by how many effective plays they're worth, not just whether the same player returns, predicts covering the spread better than the model's existing player-continuity measure. The limited data leaned against it, but more importantly, the person who reviewed this found the way 'value' was calculated has a design flaw -- about half of all team-games get treated as neutral by an accident of the math -- so this specific result describes a flawed measuring instrument, not a settled answer about whether the underlying idea works.

close_game_luck_early_season_fade.plain_summary: A team was in the top quarter of the league last season for winning close, one-score games or for turnover margin, both patterns usually attributed to luck rather than repeatable skill, and today's game falls in the first eight weeks of the new season, the point in the year with the least fresh information to override that old read. Bet against that team; the limited data so far actually leaned in the opposite direction.

close_game_luck_one_score_over_fade.plain_summary: A team won an unusually high share of close, one-score games last season relative to its overall record, a pattern usually attributed to luck rather than skill. Bet against that team this season, on the idea that a lucky close-game record won't repeat; the limited data so far came back almost exactly at a coin flip.

close_game_luck_one_score_under_rebound.plain_summary: A team won an unusually low share of close, one-score games last season relative to its overall record, the mirror image of a lucky team -- an unlucky one that might be due to bounce back. Bet on that team this season; the limited data so far came back almost exactly at a coin flip.

close_game_luck_takeaway_share_extreme_f.plain_summary: A team recovered an unusually high share of fumbles and forced turnovers last season relative to the league norm, a stat known to swing heavily on luck rather than repeatable skill (a fumble-recovery-rate stand-in was used here because the underlying data doesn't track exactly what would be ideal). Bet against that team this season; the limited data so far leaned slightly against the idea.

close_game_luck_turnover_over_fade.plain_summary: A team had an unusually strong turnover margin last season, a stat that tends to drift back toward average rather than persist as a real team skill. Bet against that team this season, on the theory a hot turnover margin won't repeat; the limited data so far came back almost exactly at a coin flip.

close_game_luck_turnover_under_rebound.plain_summary: A team had an unusually poor turnover margin last season, the mirror case of a team that might be due to bounce back toward average. Bet on that team this season; this was the strongest-leaning result among a related group of turnover- and close-game-luck checks, though it's a decomposition of the same underlying turnover-margin idea as a sibling result rather than fresh, independent confirmation of it.

combined_stacker_opener_2022_2023.plain_summary: This tests bolting four separate situational betting angles -- an injury-value matchup rule, a pre-2020 cold-weather-visitor angle, a pre-2020 warm-team-in-cold-weather angle, and a betting-line-size zone -- onto the model's production recipe all at once, checked against the plain production recipe alone at the actual Tuesday opening line, on a 2022-2023 slice of games set aside for this kind of confirmation check. The limited data leaned against the combined version, and the sample and the four extra factors overlap with other results recorded separately, so this shouldn't be read as a fresh, independent test of any one of them.

den_home_vs_own_conference.plain_summary: Denver is hosting a game against a visiting team from its own conference, opponents who make the trip to Denver's high altitude more often than most teams and so may be more used to it. The limited data leaned against the home team getting any extra benefit in these more altitude-experienced matchups.

divisional_rematch_blowout_winner_fade.plain_summary: A team is playing the rematch leg of a divisional series after having beaten this same opponent by 14 or more points earlier in the season. Bet against that team in the rematch, on the theory that a blowout invites a letdown; this is a narrower, same-opponent version of a separate blowout-letdown idea that instead looks at any 17-plus-point win over any opponent. The limited data leaned against the idea, and even flipped direction between the earlier and more recent halves of the seasons studied.

divisional_rematch_revenge_early_w1to6.plain_summary: A team is seeking revenge in the rematch leg of a divisional series, having lost the first meeting, and that rematch falls in the first six weeks of the season, an unusually early scheduling spot for a rematch. Bet on the revenge-seeking team; only 4 games in the whole period studied ever fit this specific spot, so the range reported here is really just describing that handful of games rather than a reliable estimate.

divisional_rematch_revenge_home_loser.plain_summary: A team is seeking revenge in the rematch leg of a divisional series, and its loss in the first meeting happened at its own home stadium rather than on the road. Bet on that team in the rematch; the limited data leaned toward the idea, and its edge actually showed up a bit larger than the mirror case where the earlier loss happened on the road, which runs against the intuition that a road loss should sting less.

divisional_rematch_revenge_late_w12plus.plain_summary: A team is seeking revenge in the rematch leg of a divisional series, and that rematch falls in week 12 or later, when playoff seeding stakes are higher. Bet on that team in the rematch; the limited data leaned toward the idea.

divisional_rematch_revenge_road_loser.plain_summary: A team is seeking revenge in the rematch leg of a divisional series, and its loss in the first meeting happened on the road rather than at home. Bet on that team in the rematch; the limited data leaned toward the idea, though the size of the edge swung a lot between the earlier and more recent halves of the seasons studied.

dst_arizona_away_shield.plain_summary: The Arizona Cardinals, the one NFL team whose home state never observes the twice-yearly clock change, are the VISITING team during the week of that clock change nationally, playing a home team that -- unlike Arizona -- actually had to adjust its own clocks. Bet against Arizona in this spot, on the idea that Arizona still carries ordinary travel fatigue with no clock-change benefit of its own. This is an extremely rare situation -- one of five checks in a small batch built around the twice-yearly clock change -- and by the analysts' own admission there are too few of these games across seventeen seasons to trust the usual margin-of-error range; only the raw lean should be read, and it leaned toward the idea.

dst_arizona_home_shield.plain_summary: The Arizona Cardinals, the one NFL team whose home state never observes the twice-yearly clock change, are the HOME team during the week of that clock change nationally, hosting a visiting team that -- unlike Arizona -- actually had to adjust its own clocks on top of traveling. Bet on Arizona in this spot. This is an extremely rare situation -- one of five checks in a small batch built around the twice-yearly clock change -- and by the analysts' own admission there are too few of these games across seventeen seasons to trust the usual margin-of-error range; only the raw lean should be read, and it came back almost exactly even.

dst_fall_transition_shock.plain_summary: A game falls within the first week after the fall clock change (the one where clocks 'fall back' an hour), which piles ordinary travel disruption on top of a national clock shift for the visiting team, while the home team stays in its own bed and routine. Bet on the home team; the limited data leaned against the idea.

dst_placebo_shifted_window.plain_summary: Placebo: an identical seven-day window placed three weeks before the clocks actually change, where nothing should show up. Anything it finds is noise the method invents on its own, and here it leaned slightly toward showing a pattern anyway -- a useful reminder of how much random wiggle this kind of check can produce even with nothing real going on.

dst_transition_eastbound_interaction.plain_summary: A team is both traveling east across at least two time zones for this game AND that game falls in the week of the national fall clock change, stacking ordinary jet-lag-style travel disruption on top of the clock shift. Bet on the opponent, the team not making that eastbound trip; the limited data leaned toward the idea.

ecdf_smoothing_accuracy.plain_summary: College football: tests replacing one piece of the model's internal machinery -- how it converts a raw prediction into a win probability, currently done by comparing against a jagged list of past outcomes -- with a smoothed version of the same comparison. It makes the model's probability estimates noticeably better-calibrated, a separate, already-settled finding used elsewhere, but on the project's real yardstick of picking the correct side of the spread the limited data actually leans the wrong way, so it should not be adopted for picking accuracy on that basis.

environmental_battery_aqi_high_outdoor.plain_summary: An outdoor game is played in a county where local air quality was measured as 'Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups' or worse as of the Tuesday before kickoff. Bet on the home team; this was one of two air-quality and drought checks tried together with no direction picked in advance, and the limited data leaned toward the idea, holding up similarly in both an earlier and a more recent era.

environmental_battery_aqi_high_outdoor_o.plain_summary: An outdoor game is played in a county where local air quality was measured as 'Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups' or worse as of the Tuesday before kickoff, this time checked using the actual Tuesday opening betting line instead of the closing line. Bet on the home team; only 9 games in the 2020-2025 sample qualified, so this is recorded mainly for completeness rather than as an informative estimate on its own, though it agrees in direction with the larger version of the same check.

environmental_battery_drought_severe_gra.plain_summary: An outdoor game is played on a grass field in a county experiencing at least 'severe' drought conditions covering half the county or more as of the Tuesday before kickoff, which can make the turf harder and faster. Bet on the home team; this was one of two air-quality and drought checks tried together with no direction picked in advance, and the finding actually reversed direction between an earlier era (leaning firmly against the home team) and a more recent one (leaning for it), reported as a real swing rather than smoothed into one number.

An outdoor game is played on a grass field in a county experiencing at least 'severe' drought conditions covering half the county or more, checked here as a plain exploratory reproduction rather than a directional bet -- the reported 'positive' side is a fixed bookkeeping convention, not a claim about which team benefits. The limited data leaned toward the home team, matching the more recent-era reading of a related, larger version of the same check.

era_trend_division_revenge_game.plain_summary: Not a bet itself, but a check on how the size of one specific situational edge -- a team playing its second meeting of the season against a division rival after losing the first meeting -- has drifted from season to season since 2009, using 2020-2025 as its reference point. The edge shows no reliable overall trend across seasons, though a break-point search points to it roughly halving in size somewhere around 2016, and it tends to shrink in seasons where games around the league are more lopsided.

era_trend_extra_rest_edge.plain_summary: Not a bet itself, but a check on how the size of one specific situational edge -- a team having at least four more days of rest than its opponent -- has drifted from season to season since 2009, using 2020-2025 as its reference point. The edge shows no reliable trend across seasons, though a break-point search finds a fairly stable shift from a negative to a positive edge somewhere around 2015.

era_trend_hc_year_one_fade.plain_summary: Not a bet itself, but a check on how the size of one specific situational edge -- betting against a team playing under a first-season head coach during weeks 1 through 8 -- has drifted from season to season since 2009, using 2020-2025 as its reference point. Unlike most of these era-drift checks, this one shows a real, statistically clear upward trend: the edge has been getting stronger over time, essentially appearing out of nothing before around 2018-2019 and growing large since, roughly tracking how many first-year head coaches are around the league in a given season; this pattern is used elsewhere in the project as a known, already-established benchmark case.

era_trend_home_underdog.plain_summary: Not a bet itself, but a check on how the size of one specific situational edge -- backing the home team when the betting line makes them the underdog -- has drifted from season to season since 2009, using 2020-2025 as its reference point. The edge shows no statistically reliable trend across seasons, though a break-point search suggests it may have shifted from a negative to a positive lean somewhere around 2020, roughly opposite the direction the league-wide home-field advantage itself has moved.

era_trend_penalty_rate_quartile.plain_summary: Not a bet itself, but a check on how the size of one specific situational edge -- backing a team that was flagged for penalties least often last season over one flagged most often -- has drifted from season to season since 2009, using 2020-2025 as its reference point. The edge shows no reliable trend and swings unstably between positive and negative depending on exactly where the era boundary is drawn, which looks more like noise than a real drifting effect.

era_trend_production_model_opener_proxy_.plain_summary: Not a single-game bet: this tracks how the live prediction model's own overall picking edge against a coin flip has drifted season by season since 2009, using 2020-2025, the true Tuesday-opener-graded years, as its reference point. The edge shows a real, statistically clear upward trend over time, but the analysts flag an important caveat: the way games were graded changed exactly at the 2019/2020 boundary (an older market-based stand-in for the opening line before 2020, the real opening line from 2020 on), so this apparent growth can't be cleanly separated from that change in measurement method.

era_trend_surface_switch.plain_summary: Not a bet itself, but a check on how the size of one specific situational edge -- a visiting team whose own home field is grass playing today on artificial turf -- has drifted from season to season since 2009, using 2020-2025 as its reference point. The edge shows no reliable trend, and its estimated turning point isn't consistent from one resample of the data to the next, which looks more like noise than a real drifting effect.

era_weighting_cfb_half_life_16.plain_summary: College football: tests changing a setting in the prediction model so older seasons count less and less toward its training, halving their influence every 16 seasons, compared with the model's default of weighting every past season equally. The limited data leaned toward this change being an improvement.

era_weighting_cfb_half_life_2.plain_summary: College football: tests changing a setting in the prediction model so older seasons count less and less toward its training, halving their influence every 2 seasons -- a very fast fade toward only recent data -- compared with the model's default of weighting every past season equally. The limited data leaned toward this change being an improvement.

era_weighting_cfb_half_life_4.plain_summary: College football: tests changing a setting in the prediction model so older seasons count less and less toward its training, halving their influence every 4 seasons, compared with the model's default of weighting every past season equally. The limited data leaned toward this change being an improvement.

era_weighting_cfb_half_life_8.plain_summary: College football: tests changing a setting in the prediction model so older seasons count less and less toward its training, halving their influence every 8 seasons, compared with the model's default of weighting every past season equally. The limited data leaned toward this change being an improvement, one of the stronger-leaning settings in a sweep of several half-life values tried together.

era_weighting_cfb_rolling_10.plain_summary: College football: tests training the prediction model only on the most recent 10 seasons of data, discarding anything older entirely, compared with the model's default of using and equally weighting every past season. The limited data leaned against this change.

era_weighting_cfb_rolling_6.plain_summary: College football: tests training the prediction model only on the most recent 6 seasons of data, discarding anything older entirely, compared with the model's default of using and equally weighting every past season. The limited data leaned mildly toward this change being an improvement.

era_weighting_half_life_8_opener_confirm.plain_summary: This is a planned follow-up confirmation, checked at the actual Tuesday opening line, of a model setting that had looked promising in earlier screening: making older seasons count less and less toward training, halving their influence every 8 seasons, versus the model's default of weighting every season equally. This confirmation -- the fourth time this exact setting had been examined, and on a set of games overlapping a prior look, so not a fresh independent check -- came back leaning against the change, in contrast to the more encouraging earlier screens.

era_weighting_nfl_half_life_16.plain_summary: Tests changing a setting in the prediction model so older seasons count less and less toward its training, halving their influence every 16 seasons, compared with the model's default of weighting every past season equally, checked at the closing betting line and run only because a similar college-football check had already leaned positive. The limited data leaned toward this change being an improvement.

era_weighting_nfl_half_life_2.plain_summary: Tests changing a setting in the prediction model so older seasons count less and less toward its training, halving their influence every 2 seasons -- a very fast fade toward only recent data -- compared with the model's default of weighting every past season equally, checked at the closing betting line and run only because a similar college-football check had already leaned positive. The limited data leaned toward this change being an improvement.

era_weighting_nfl_half_life_4.plain_summary: Tests changing a setting in the prediction model so older seasons count less and less toward its training, halving their influence every 4 seasons, compared with the model's default of weighting every past season equally, checked at the closing betting line and run only because a similar college-football check had already leaned positive. The limited data leaned toward this change being an improvement.
