era_weighting_nfl_half_life_8.plain_summary: Tests changing a setting in the prediction model so older seasons count less and less toward its training, halving their influence every 8 seasons, compared with the model's default of weighting every past season equally, checked at the closing betting line and run only because a similar college-football check had already leaned positive. The limited data leaned toward this change being an improvement, the strongest-leaning of the half-life settings tried at the closing line.

era_weighting_nfl_half_life_8_opener.plain_summary: An early, non-final look at the same model setting as its own later confirmation test -- making older seasons count less and less toward training, halving their influence every 8 seasons -- checked here at the actual Tuesday opening line rather than the closing line. Unlike the encouraging closing-line screens that came before it, this opener-graded look leaned against the change, while a separate check at the closing line on an overlapping set of games leaned the opposite way -- a genuine disagreement the analysts chose to report rather than paper over.

era_weighting_nfl_rolling_10.plain_summary: Tests training the prediction model only on the most recent 10 seasons of data, discarding anything older entirely, compared with the model's default of using and equally weighting every past season, checked at the closing betting line and run only because a similar college-football check had already leaned positive. The limited data leaned toward this change being an improvement.

era_weighting_nfl_rolling_6.plain_summary: Tests training the prediction model only on the most recent 6 seasons of data, discarding anything older entirely, compared with the model's default of using and equally weighting every past season, checked at the closing betting line and run only because a similar college-football check had already leaned positive. The limited data came back close to a coin flip, leaning only very slightly toward the change.

estimation_variance_bagging_stability_cf.plain_summary: College football: tests averaging many slightly different refits of the model together, each trained on a random resample of the same games, rather than trusting a single fit -- a technique aimed at making the model's picks more stable from one run to the next, not necessarily at finding a bigger edge. The clearest result was that this noticeably cut down how often the model's pick for a game flipped between runs; the effect on picking accuracy itself was real but modest and doesn't by itself meet the bar for switching to this approach live, so it's recommended as good practice for testing future ideas rather than a change affecting any pick made today.

estimation_variance_center_shrink_cfb.plain_summary: College football: tests nudging the model's predicted point spread partway back toward the actual betting line before turning it into a win probability, checked across five different nudge amounts. The best of the five settings came back barely on the positive side of a coin flip, and the analysts are explicit that this near-zero result is the least-bad of several unpromising options rather than a real discovery -- recorded because the project's rule is to keep every inconclusive result on the books, not because it looked promising.

estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_fu.plain_summary: College football: not a new betting angle -- this tests a general design principle for building future prediction features, checking whether a model does better by only acting on picks where it clearly disagrees with a simpler baseline model, deferring to that baseline otherwise, rather than letting every feature influence every pick. The idea tested well, leaning strongly positive, but it's explicitly a lesson about how to evaluate future model changes, not a new feature to add or a pick to play.

estimation_variance_disagreement_gate_ta.plain_summary: College football: a planned follow-up confirmation, on a fresh set of games not used in the original test, of the design idea that a model should only override a simpler baseline on picks where it clearly disagrees with that baseline -- tested here against a required 'do-nothing' comparison that applies the same kind of override at random. On this new set of games the result actually leaned the wrong way and did not repeat the earlier promising result, though not cleanly enough to call the idea disproven; the fact that it still beat the random-override comparison is the one piece of this check that still points toward the idea being real rather than arbitrary.

ffc_adp_cellA_highadp_underdog_back_ppr_.plain_summary: In weeks 1 through 4 of the season, under fantasy-football scoring that counts receptions (PPR), a team's roster ranks in the top third of the league by how highly fantasy drafters valued its offensive skill players before the season, and the betting market has that team as an underdog anyway. Bet on that team, the fantasy-favored crowd's pick, to cover; the limited data leaned toward the idea, though this uses a snapshot of preseason fantasy rankings that is never refreshed during the season, and a break-even calculation shows the measured edge is not yet large enough to clear the cost of betting even if it holds up.

ffc_adp_cellB_adpwins_residual_pos_back_.plain_summary: In weeks 1 through 4 of the season, under fantasy-football scoring that counts receptions (PPR), one specific team stands out as ranked unusually high by preseason fantasy drafters relative to how many games it actually won last year -- a sign the fantasy crowd may be more excited about the roster than results justify. Bet on that team, following the fantasy crowd's enthusiasm; the limited data leaned against the idea.

ffc_adp_cellC_highadp_underdog_back_ppr_.plain_summary: In just weeks 1 and 2 of the season, under fantasy-football scoring that counts receptions (PPR), a team's roster ranks in the top third of the league by how highly fantasy drafters valued its offensive skill players before the season, and the betting market has that team as an underdog anyway. Bet on that team; this is a narrower, even-earlier-season repeat of a related four-week check and pointed the same direction, though with less data behind it.

ffc_adp_cellD_adpwins_residual_pos_back_.plain_summary: In just weeks 1 and 2 of the season, under fantasy-football scoring that counts receptions (PPR), one specific team stands out as ranked unusually high by preseason fantasy drafters relative to how many games it actually won last year. Bet on that team, following the fantasy crowd's enthusiasm; this is a narrower, even-earlier-season repeat of a related four-week check, and it also leaned against the idea.

ffc_adp_robust_std_cellA_highadp_underdo.plain_summary: In weeks 1 through 4 of the season, under standard (non-reception-counting) fantasy-football scoring, a team's roster ranks in the top third of the league by how highly fantasy drafters valued its offensive skill players before the season, and the betting market has that team as an underdog anyway. Bet on that team; this is a scoring-format check of a related idea originally tested under reception-counting (PPR) fantasy scoring, and the edge came back noticeably smaller here, suggesting part of the original finding may be specific to PPR leagues.

ffc_adp_robust_std_cellB_adpwins_residua.plain_summary: In weeks 1 through 4 of the season, under standard (non-reception-counting) fantasy-football scoring, one specific team stands out as ranked unusually high by preseason fantasy drafters relative to how many games it actually won last year. Bet on that team, following the fantasy crowd's enthusiasm; this is a scoring-format check of a related idea originally tested under reception-counting (PPR) fantasy scoring, and it leaned against the idea in both formats.

fluview_away_market_elevated.plain_summary: Flu is running at its yearly peak in the visiting team's home state. Bet on the home team.

fluview_differential_home_worse.plain_summary: Comparing games where flu levels are unusually high in exactly one team's home state but not the other's, this looks specifically at the case where the home team's own state has the elevated flu and the visiting team's does not. Bet against the home team; the limited data came back close to a coin flip, only slightly leaning against the idea, and this particular split has a much smaller sample of games than the plainer single-team versions of the same idea.

fluview_home_market_elevated.plain_summary: Flu is running at an unusually high level in the home team's own state as of the Tuesday before kickoff. Bet against the home team; the limited data leaned toward the idea.

fluview_peak_away_elevated.plain_summary: During the weeks of the season when nationwide flu activity is typically at its highest, flu is also running at an unusually high level specifically in the visiting team's home state. Bet on the home team; the limited data came back almost exactly at a coin flip.

fluview_peak_home_elevated.plain_summary: During the weeks of the season when nationwide flu activity is typically at its highest, flu is also running at an unusually high level specifically in the home team's own state. Bet against the home team; the limited data leaned toward the idea.

forecast_weather_dome_team_outdoors_cold.plain_summary: A team that normally plays its home games in a dome is on the road today in an outdoor stadium, and the pregame Tuesday forecast calls for 40 degrees or colder -- checked using the forecast available days before kickoff rather than the weather that actually occurred, so it reflects information a bettor could really have used. Bet on the home team; the limited data leaned against the idea, and it draws on a somewhat smaller, more recent set of games than the related version of this check that used the actual game-day weather instead of the forecast.

forecast_weather_high_wind_outdoor.plain_summary: An outdoor game has a pregame Tuesday forecast calling for wind of 15 miles per hour or more -- checked using the forecast available days before kickoff, so it reflects information a bettor could really have used, with no side picked in advance for which team benefits. The limited data came back close to a coin flip, leaning only slightly against the home team, and draws on a somewhat smaller, more recent set of games than the related version of this check that used the actual game-day wind instead of the forecast.

forecast_weather_kn_dome_cold_windy_full.plain_summary: A team that normally plays its home games in a dome is on the road today in an outdoor stadium, and the forecast closest to actual kickoff calls for 32 degrees or colder with wind of at least 10 miles per hour -- a stricter, cold-and-windy version of a related cold-only check, using the most up-to-date forecast rather than one taken days out. The limited data leaned against the home team getting any extra benefit from the tougher conditions.

forecast_weather_kn_dome_cold_windy_pre2.plain_summary: A team that normally plays its home games in a dome is on the road today in an outdoor stadium, and the forecast closest to actual kickoff calls for 32 degrees or colder with wind of at least 10 miles per hour, checked here only across seasons 2009 through 2019. The limited data leaned against the home team getting any extra benefit, similar to the same check run across the full range of seasons.

forecast_weather_kn_precip_high_total_fu.plain_summary: An outdoor game has a forecast, taken closest to actual kickoff, calling for at least a 60% chance of rain or snow, and the combined point total set by the market is unusually high at 47 points or more -- on the theory that a high total suggests the market hasn't fully priced in how much precipitation usually suppresses scoring, and that home teams generally handle their own site's weather better. Bet on the home team; the limited data leaned toward the idea.

forecast_weather_kn_precip_high_total_pr.plain_summary: An outdoor game has a forecast, taken closest to actual kickoff, calling for at least a 60% chance of rain or snow, and the combined point total set by the market is unusually high at 47 points or more, checked here only across seasons 2009 through 2019. Bet on the home team; the limited data leaned toward the idea, similar to the same check run across the full range of seasons.

forecast_weather_kn_temp_gap_cold_visito.plain_summary: The visiting team's own typical home climate is far warmer than the forecast closest to actual kickoff for today's outdoor game -- specifically, a drop of 25 degrees or more from what that team is used to. Bet on the home team, on the idea that a sharp weather shock away from a visitor's usual climate is disruptive; the limited data leaned toward the idea.

The visiting team's own typical home climate is far warmer than the forecast closest to actual kickoff for today's outdoor game -- specifically, a drop of 25 degrees or more from what that team is used to -- checked here only across seasons 2009 through 2019. Bet on the home team; the limited data leaned toward the idea, similar to the same check run across the full range of seasons.

best_pick_opener_ranker_dispersion_filte.plain_summary: This compares two ways of choosing the week's marquee 'Best Pick' game: one that only considers games where the betting markets most agree with each other before ranking by the model's confidence, against a version that ranks all games that way with no such filter. Checked on a stretch of 1,537 games and 107 weeks already reused for two earlier related checks this same session, so the result carries less weight than a fresh sample would; the limited data leaned toward the filtered version, though a different chooser built on the same pool of games moved in the opposite direction, so this does not change which rule the project actually uses.

best_pick_tiebreak_cfb_stage0_ecdf_gauss.plain_summary: College football: this is a preliminary check of one way to break ties when two games are equally strong candidates for the week's marquee 'Best Pick' -- ranking tied games by a smoothed probability-distance method instead of simple alphabetical order. In college football, 'alphabetical' order actually turned out to correlate strongly with the outcome on its own (because game ID numbers aren't random), which muddies this specific test; the real test of this idea is a separate check using NFL data. The limited data here leaned strongly against the smoothed method.

bias_battery_backup_qb_start.plain_summary: A team is starting a quarterback who isn't the one who has taken most of its snaps this season (at least three starts already banked by the usual starter) -- typically a backup stepping in for an injured or benched starter. Checked as one of 17 similar situational checks tried together in a single batch, these games leaned toward the backup-led team covering the spread less often than the rest of the slate, though the effect actually ran the opposite way in the two eras studied separately (negative from 2009-2017, positive from 2018-2025).

bias_battery_backup_qb_start_opener.plain_summary: A team is starting a quarterback who isn't the one who has taken most of its snaps this season, checked using the season's opening betting lines instead of the lines closer to kickoff. This is a repeat, opener-graded look at an already-recorded finding, logged mainly to track its direction rather than as a fresh result on its own, and it leaned toward the backup-led team covering less often than the rest of the slate.

bias_battery_bad_team_late.plain_summary: A team has been eliminated from realistic playoff contention, having won 30% or less of its games so far, and it's week 11 or later in the season. Checked as one of 17 similar situational checks tried together in a single batch, these teams leaned toward covering the spread slightly less often than the rest of that week's slate.

bias_battery_december_weather_dogs.plain_summary: A home team is an underdog, it's week 14 or later, the game is outdoors or with the roof open, and the temperature is 32 degrees Fahrenheit or colder. Checked as one of 17 similar situational checks tried together in a single batch, these cold-weather home underdogs leaned strongly toward covering the spread less often than the rest of that week's slate.

bias_battery_division_revenge_game.plain_summary: A team is playing its division rival for the second time this season, after losing to that same rival in their first meeting. Checked as one of 17 similar situational checks tried together in a single batch, these teams seeking revenge leaned toward covering the spread more often than the rest of that week's slate.

bias_battery_division_revenge_game_opene.plain_summary: A team is playing the same opponent for the second time this season, after losing the first meeting, checked using the season's opening betting lines rather than the lines closer to kickoff. This is a repeat, opener-graded look at an already-recorded finding, logged mainly to track its direction rather than as a fresh result on its own, and it leaned toward the team seeking revenge covering more often than the rest of the slate.

bias_battery_extra_rest_edge.plain_summary: A team has at least four more days of rest than its opponent heading into the game. Checked as one of 17 similar situational checks tried together in a single batch, these better-rested teams came back essentially a coin flip against the rest of that week's slate.

bias_battery_extra_rest_edge_opener.plain_summary: A team has at least four more days of rest than its opponent, checked using the season's opening betting lines rather than the lines closer to kickoff. This is a repeat, opener-graded look at an already-recorded finding, logged mainly to track its direction rather than as a fresh result on its own, and it leaned toward the better-rested team covering less often than the rest of the slate.

bias_battery_great_team_late.plain_summary: A team has effectively locked up its playoff seed already, with an 80% or better win rate so far, in the final stretch of the season (weeks 15 through 18) when a team might ease off. Checked as one of 17 similar situational checks tried together in a single batch, these teams leaned toward covering the spread slightly less often than the rest of that week's slate.

bias_battery_home_underdog.plain_summary: The home team is getting points, meaning the betting market favors the visiting team. Checked as one of 17 similar situational checks tried together in a single batch, these home underdogs came back an almost exact coin flip against the rest of that week's slate.

bias_battery_home_underdog_opener.plain_summary: The home team is getting points at the season's opening betting line, before the market has a chance to move. This is a repeat, opener-graded look at an already-recorded finding, logged mainly to track its direction rather than as a fresh result on its own, and it leaned slightly toward the home underdog covering more often than the rest of the slate.

bias_battery_large_favorite.plain_summary: A team is favored by more than 10 points. Checked as one of 17 similar situational checks tried together in a single batch, these heavy favorites leaned toward covering the spread less often than the rest of that week's slate.

bias_battery_marquee_favorite.plain_summary: One of the four teams believed to draw the heaviest public betting interest -- the Cowboys, Packers, Steelers, or Patriots -- is favored to win. Checked as one of 17 similar situational checks tried together in a single batch, these popular favorites leaned strongly toward covering the spread less often than the rest of that week's slate.

bias_battery_motivation_mismatch.plain_summary: A team that is still competitive, winning 40% or more of its games, is facing an opponent already eliminated from realistic playoff contention late in the season. Checked as one of 17 similar situational checks tried together in a single batch, the still-competitive team leaned toward covering the spread less often than the rest of that week's slate.

bias_battery_motivation_mismatch_opener.plain_summary: A team that is still competitive is facing an opponent already eliminated from realistic playoff contention late in the season, checked using the season's opening betting lines rather than the lines closer to kickoff. This is a repeat, opener-graded look at an already-recorded finding, logged mainly to track its direction rather than as a fresh result on its own, and it came back close to a coin flip.

bias_battery_post_blowout_loss_bounce.plain_summary: A team lost its previous game by 17 points or more. Checked as one of 17 similar situational checks tried together in a single batch, teams in this bounce-back spot leaned toward covering the spread more often than the rest of that week's slate, though the sample is small.

bias_battery_post_blowout_win_letdown.plain_summary: A team won its previous game by 17 points or more, the kind of spot where a 'letdown' the following week is often assumed. Checked as one of 17 similar situational checks tried together in a single batch, teams in this spot actually leaned toward covering the spread more often than the rest of that week's slate, the opposite of what a letdown theory would predict, though the sample is small.

bias_battery_primetime_favorite.plain_summary: A team is favored to win in a Thursday, Monday, or Sunday-night nationally televised game (Saturday games are not included in this check). Checked as one of 17 similar situational checks tried together in a single batch, these primetime favorites came back close to a coin flip against the rest of that week's slate.

bias_battery_sandwich_spot.plain_summary: A team is playing a non-division opponent that's sandwiched between division games the week before and the week after -- a classic 'trap game' spot. Checked as one of 17 similar situational checks tried together in a single batch, teams in this spot leaned toward covering the spread more often than the rest of that week's slate.

bias_battery_sandwich_spot_opener.plain_summary: A team is playing a non-division opponent sandwiched between division games the week before and after, checked using the season's opening betting lines rather than the lines closer to kickoff. This is a repeat, opener-graded look at an already-recorded finding, logged mainly to track its direction rather than as a fresh result on its own, and it leaned toward covering less often than the rest of the slate.

bias_battery_short_week.plain_summary: A team is playing on short rest, five days or less since its last game. Checked as one of 17 similar situational checks tried together in a single batch on a very large sample, these teams leaned strongly toward covering the spread less often than the rest of that week's slate, and the effect was even more one-sided in the 2009-2017 seasons specifically.

bias_battery_short_week_opener.plain_summary: A team is playing on short rest, five days or less since its last game, checked using the season's opening betting lines rather than the lines closer to kickoff. This is a repeat, opener-graded look at an already-recorded finding, logged mainly to track its direction rather than as a fresh result on its own, and here it leaned about as strongly as this kind of check can toward the short-rested team covering less often than the rest of the slate.

nflcom_refresh_out2_starters_on_chain.plain_summary: The team's own final NFL.com injury report, checked Friday or Saturday before the game, lists two or more starting-caliber players as out. This is layered on top of several other adjustments already made to the model's picks (a coach-experience fade and a player-arrests flip) as one combined package, and betting against the banged-up team added real value over that package alone across 2022-2024 games.

nflcom_refresh_out2_starters_on_chain_ga.plain_summary: The team's own final NFL.com injury report lists two or more starting-caliber players as out, checked only using report pages confirmed to have actually posted before that specific game's pick deadline (an earlier version of this check accidentally used some reports published after kickoff). Betting against the banged-up team, layered on top of a package of other model adjustments, still added value once that timing mistake was fixed, though the edge shrank slightly.

observed_movement_oracle_full_slate.plain_summary: Not a real bet: this is a best-case ceiling check that assumes perfect foresight of which way the betting line will move between the Tuesday opener and the final closing number, then always follows that direction. It shows how much value would be on the table if that movement were known in advance and layered on top of the model's regular picks, across 1,503 games from 2020 through 2025 -- real production never has this information before kickoff.

observed_movement_oracle_sunday_am_reali.plain_summary: Not a fully real bet: this checks how much value would be captured by always following the direction the betting line had already moved toward by roughly 11 a.m. Eastern on game day, the latest market snapshot this project's data actually captures for Sunday games, applied across 799 games from 2023 through 2025. Because Sunday-afternoon and Sunday-night market moves after that point aren't captured in this data, the number is described as a floor, not the true ceiling, on what a fully real-time system could capture.

observed_movement_threshold_0_5.plain_summary: A rule that starts from the model's usual pick, then switches sides only if the betting line moves at least half a point from Tuesday's opening number toward the other side by the time it closes, otherwise leaving the pick alone. Checked across 1,503 games from 2020 through 2025, most games saw a big enough move to be eligible, though the market had already agreed with the model's original pick more than half the time even before any flip; because it uses the closing line, this version may overstate how early some of that information is actually available before kickoff.

observed_movement_threshold_0_5_sunday_a.plain_summary: A rule that starts from the model's usual pick and switches sides only if the betting line has already moved at least half a point from Tuesday's opening number by roughly 11 a.m. Eastern on game day, the latest market snapshot this project's data actually captures for Sunday games, otherwise leaving the pick alone. Checked across 799 games from 2023 through 2025, most of which saw enough movement to be eligible for a possible flip.

observed_movement_threshold_1_0.plain_summary: A rule that starts from the model's usual pick, then switches sides only if the betting line moves at least a full point from Tuesday's opening number by the time it closes, a tighter trigger than the same idea with a half-point threshold. Checked across 1,503 games from 2020 through 2025, about 44% of games saw enough movement to be eligible, and the limited data leaned toward this being worth doing; because it uses the closing line, this version may overstate how early some of that information is actually available before kickoff.

observed_movement_threshold_1_0_sunday_a.plain_summary: A rule that starts from the model's usual pick and switches sides only if the betting line has already moved at least a full point from Tuesday's opening number by roughly 11 a.m. Eastern on game day, the latest market snapshot this project's data actually captures for Sunday games, otherwise leaving the pick alone. Checked across 799 games from 2023 through 2025, this was the strongest-leaning of several movement-threshold checks tried in this family.

odds_microstructure_H1_1_2_dose_response.plain_summary: This compares how accurate a betting-market-confidence-based pick is between the third of games where the market is leaning hardest toward one side and the third of games where it's leaning the least, rather than comparing either group to a plain coin flip. It's one of 14 cells tried together as an exploratory scan of market microstructure, and the limited data leaned toward the least-confident group actually being more accurate, the opposite of what you'd expect if stronger market conviction meant a more reliable signal.

odds_microstructure_H2_2a_spread_std_abs.plain_summary: This compares how far off the final score margin lands from the point spread, measured in points, between games where different sportsbooks disagree with each other the most on the spread versus the least -- not a pick-accuracy percentage but a measure of point-margin surprise. It's one of 14 cells tried together as an exploratory scan of market microstructure, and the limited data leaned toward games with more cross-book disagreement seeing bigger point-spread misses.

odds_microstructure_H2_2b_price_std_juic.plain_summary: This compares how accurate a betting-market-confidence-based pick is between games where the odds (the price charged on either side, not the point spread) are quoted very similarly across sportsbooks versus games where they vary a lot, rather than comparing either group to a plain coin flip. It's one of 14 cells tried together as an exploratory scan of market microstructure, and the limited data leaned toward the more-consistent-odds group actually being less accurate.

odds_microstructure_H3_3_0a_full_week_or.plain_summary: Not a real bet: this is a best-case, perfect-foresight check of how accurate always picking the side the betting line ultimately moved toward would have been, across a full week of games from 2020 through 2025, used as a sanity check on the modeling pipeline rather than a playable idea. It came back well above a coin flip, as expected for something built with hindsight.

odds_microstructure_H3_3_0b_full_week_or.plain_summary: Not a real bet: this is a perfect-foresight check of how accurate always picking the side the betting line ultimately moved toward would have been, narrowed to the 2023 through 2025 seasons, used as a sanity-check baseline rather than a playable idea. It came back well above a coin flip, as expected for something built with hindsight.

odds_microstructure_H3_3_1_tue_to_wed_or.plain_summary: Not a real bet: this is a perfect-foresight check of how accurate always picking the side the betting line moved toward would have been, using only the smaller amount of movement that happens between Tuesday's opening line and the following Wednesday, across 2023 through 2025 games. Even this narrow early-week window of hindsight movement came back well above a coin flip.

odds_microstructure_H5_5_1_totals_juice_.plain_summary: This checks how accurate a betting-market-confidence-based pick is on the over/under total-points market, rather than the against-the-spread market this project otherwise focuses on. It's one of 14 cells tried together as an exploratory scan of market microstructure, and the limited data leaned toward this being worth something, though it remains a small, unconfirmed slice of a larger mined batch.

odds_microstructure_H6_6_1_abs_ats_margi.plain_summary: This compares how far off the final score margin lands from the point spread, measured in points, between games where the sportsbook's own cut (the 'hold,' the gap between what it charges on each side) is highest versus lowest -- not a pick-accuracy percentage but a measure of point-margin surprise. It's one of 14 cells tried together as an exploratory scan of market microstructure, and the limited data leaned toward high-hold games actually seeing smaller point-spread misses, not bigger ones.

odds_microstructure_H6_6_2_juice_accurac.plain_summary: This compares how accurate a betting-market-confidence-based pick is between games where the sportsbook's own cut (the 'hold,' the gap between what it charges on each side) is highest versus lowest, rather than comparing either group to a plain coin flip. It's one of 14 cells tried together as an exploratory scan of market microstructure, and the limited data leaned toward high-hold games actually being less accurate, not more.

offseason_retention_050_cfb.plain_summary: College football: this tests lowering one of the model's own settings -- how much of each team's strength rating carries over from last season -- from the default 67% down to 50%, tried as one point on a seven-value grid search. The limited data leaned firmly against this lower setting, suggesting the model should trust last season's information more, not less.

offseason_retention_075_cfb.plain_summary: College football: this tests raising one of the model's own settings -- how much of each team's strength rating carries over from last season -- from the default 67% up to 75%, tried as one point on a seven-value grid search. The limited data leaned toward this higher setting being an improvement, and the project's own notes flag this general direction, carrying over even more, as the most promising one left to explore.

ol_acute_overhaul_fade.plain_summary: A team's offensive line lost most of its usual starters (two or fewer of the normal five) between its most recent game and this one, checked as a possible fade of that team. Very few games in the data actually meet this exact bar (only 39), so the result is too small a sample to read anything into either way.

ol_high_continuity_back.plain_summary: A team's offensive line has kept the same starting group intact over its last two games, checked as a possible bet on that team for the stability. The limited data actually leaned against the idea, and it sits awkwardly next to a related check on the opposite end of line continuity that came back essentially flat, so this family of offensive-line-continuity checks doesn't hang together cleanly yet.

ol_low_continuity_fade.plain_summary: A team's offensive line has been shuffled a lot over its last two games (in the bottom quarter of teams for keeping the same starters together), checked as a possible fade of that team. The limited data came back almost exactly even, and the underlying trait of 'a shuffled line' is fairly consistent game-to-game within one season but barely carries over from one season to the next for the same team.

ol_prior_season_weak_early_fade.plain_summary: A team had a lot of offensive-line shuffling last season (bottom quarter of teams for keeping starters together), checked as a possible fade of that team in the first eight weeks of the following season, before this year's own line continuity has had time to establish itself. The limited data leaned slightly toward the idea, but the trait barely carries over from one season to the next for the same team, so a real effect here was always likely to be small.

opener_error_mining_confidence_bucket_0p.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate in games where the model itself was only slightly confident (its estimated cover probability was 2 to 5 percentage points away from a coin flip), one of several confidence-level slices checked together as an audit of the model's own calibration rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned toward the model doing better than usual in this particular confidence band.

This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate in games where the model's estimated cover probability was 5 to 10 percentage points away from a coin flip, one of several confidence-level slices checked together as an audit of the model's own calibration rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned toward the model actually doing worse than usual in this particular confidence band.

opener_error_mining_confidence_bucket_gt.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate in its most confident games, where the estimated cover probability was more than 10 percentage points away from a coin flip, one of several confidence-level slices checked together as an audit of the model's own calibration rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned toward the model doing better than usual on its most confident picks, the direction you'd hope for.

opener_error_mining_confidence_bucket_lt.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate in its least confident games, where the estimated cover probability was within 2 percentage points of a coin flip, one of several confidence-level slices checked together as an audit of the model's own calibration rather than a new betting rule. The limited data came back close to even for this near-toss-up group.

opener_error_mining_division_game_yes.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate specifically in division games, between the same four rivals who play each other every year, as an audit of where the model's current picks already run hot or cold rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned toward the model actually doing worse than usual on division games.

opener_error_mining_favorite_side_home_f.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate specifically in games where the home team is favored by the betting line, as an audit of where the model's current picks already run hot or cold rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned toward the model doing worse than usual when the home team is favored.

opener_error_mining_favorite_side_road_f.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate specifically in games where the visiting team is favored by the betting line, as an audit of where the model's current picks already run hot or cold rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned toward the model doing better than usual when the road team is favored.

opener_error_mining_movement_agreement_a.plain_summary: This entry's name says it measures games where the betting line moved toward the model's picked side, but its own record now flags a labeling mix-up meaning it actually holds the numbers for the opposite population -- games where the line moved away from the model's pick. It's kept in the registry only as an audit trail pointing to a correctly labeled version elsewhere, and should not be read at face value from its name alone.

This is the corrected version of a mislabeled diagnostic: it checks the prediction model's existing hit rate specifically in games where the betting line's move between the Tuesday opener and closing had already gone toward the side the model picked, as an audit of where the model's picks already run hot or cold. The limited data leaned strongly toward the model doing better than usual when the market agreed with its pick's direction.

opener_error_mining_movement_agreement_d.plain_summary: This entry's name says it measures games where the betting line moved away from the model's picked side, but its own record now flags a labeling mix-up meaning it actually holds the numbers for the opposite population -- games where the line moved toward the model's pick. It's kept in the registry only as an audit trail pointing to a correctly labeled version elsewhere, and should not be read at face value from its name alone.

This is the corrected version of a mislabeled diagnostic: it checks the prediction model's existing hit rate specifically in games where the betting line's move between the Tuesday opener and closing had already gone away from the side the model picked, as an audit of where the model's picks already run hot or cold. The limited data leaned strongly toward the model doing worse than usual when the market moved against its pick's direction -- exactly the population worth testing whether flipping to follow the market would help.

The betting line has already moved, between the Tuesday opening number and the closing number, away from the side the model's usual pick was on. This tests actually flipping the pick to follow that movement, only within games where this disagreement happens, compared with sticking to the model's original pick on the same games. The limited data leaned toward flipping being the better choice, and a cross-check shows this result lines up with a separate, already-recorded full-slate version of the same idea.

The betting line has already moved by at least a full point, between the Tuesday opening number and the closing number, away from the side the model's usual pick was on. This tests actually flipping the pick to follow that movement, restricted to this stronger-movement subset, compared with sticking to the model's original pick on the same games. The limited data leaned toward flipping being the better choice, and a cross-check shows this result lines up almost exactly with a separate, already-recorded full-slate version of the same one-point-threshold idea.

opener_error_mining_movement_agreement_f.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate specifically in games where the betting line didn't move at all between the Tuesday opener and closing, as an audit of where the model's current picks already run hot or cold rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned toward the model doing better than usual when the line stayed completely flat.

opener_error_mining_pick_home_away_home.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate specifically on the games where it picked the home team, as an audit of where the model's current picks already run hot or cold rather than a new betting rule. The limited data came back close to even for the model's home picks.

opener_error_mining_pick_side_favorite.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate specifically on the games where it picked the market favorite rather than the underdog, as an audit of where the model's current picks already run hot or cold rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned toward the model doing better than usual when it picks favorites.

opener_error_mining_rest_diff_away_more_.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate specifically in games where the visiting team has had more rest days than the home team, as an audit of where the model's current picks already run hot or cold rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned toward the model doing noticeably worse than usual in this situation.

opener_error_mining_rest_diff_even.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate specifically in games where both teams have had the same amount of rest, as an audit of where the model's current picks already run hot or cold rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned toward the model doing better than usual when rest is even.

opener_error_mining_season_2025.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate specifically in the 2025 season alone, as an audit of where the model's current picks already run hot or cold rather than a new betting rule. Based on only about 18 weeks of data, the limited data leaned toward the model doing worse than usual this season, though a single season is a very small sample to read much into.

opener_error_mining_slate_primetime.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate specifically in primetime games (Thursday or Monday night, or a Saturday/Sunday kickoff at 8 p.m. Eastern or later) compared with the rest of the schedule, as an audit of where the model's current picks already run hot or cold rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned toward the model doing noticeably better than usual in the primetime spotlight.

opener_error_mining_spread_magnitude_0_2.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate specifically in close games, where the opening point spread was 2.5 points or less, as an audit of where the model's current picks already run hot or cold rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned toward the model doing better than usual in these near-even games.

opener_error_mining_spread_magnitude_10p.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate specifically in blowout-line games, where the opening point spread was 10 points or more, as an audit of where the model's current picks already run hot or cold rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned strongly toward the model doing worse than usual in these lopsided games.

opener_error_mining_spread_magnitude_3_6.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate specifically in games where the opening point spread was between 3 and 6.5 points, as an audit of where the model's current picks already run hot or cold rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned toward the model doing better than usual in this middle range of spreads.

opener_error_mining_spread_magnitude_7_9.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate specifically in games where the opening point spread was between 7 and 9.5 points, as an audit of where the model's current picks already run hot or cold rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned toward the model doing worse than usual in this range of spreads.

opener_error_mining_total_bucket_45_48.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate specifically in games where the over/under total-points line was set between 45 and 48, one of several scoring-total slices checked together as an audit of where the model's current picks already run hot or cold rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned toward the model doing worse than usual in this range.

opener_error_mining_total_bucket_below_4.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate specifically in the lowest-scoring-projected games, where the over/under total-points line was set below 42, one of several scoring-total slices checked together as an audit of where the model's current picks already run hot or cold rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned toward the model doing better than usual in these low-scoring matchups.

opener_error_mining_week_third_early.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate specifically in the first third of the season, roughly weeks 1 through 6, as an audit of where the model's current picks already run hot or cold rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned toward the model doing better than usual early in the season.

opener_error_mining_week_third_late.plain_summary: This diagnostic checks whether the prediction model's existing picks have been more or less accurate specifically in the final third of the season, roughly weeks 13 through 18, as an audit of where the model's current picks already run hot or cold rather than a new betting rule. The limited data leaned toward the model doing worse than usual late in the season.

overlay_single_addition_to_played_union_.plain_summary: Not a bet itself, but a test of the process for picking a fifth ingredient to add to the four adjustments already layered onto the model's picks (a coach-experience fade, a division-rematch tilt, a player-arrests flip, and a spread-gap fade): a new addition was chosen using only 2020-2022 games, then applied unchanged to the untouched 2023-2025 games to see if the selection process itself holds up going forward. The specific addition chosen this way, a first-year head coach's very first game with that team, produced exactly zero measured difference on the holdout games; two other candidates that looked promising were deliberately not adopted because they only looked good after the fact, and both remain open ideas for future testing.

overlay_stack_combined_opener_2020_2025.plain_summary: This tests what happens if six separate experimental adjustments to the model's picks -- covering a coach-experience fade, an injury-value fade, a division-rematch tilt, a backup-quarterback fade, a playing-surface-switch tilt, and a spread-gap fade -- are all applied together at once, flipping a pick whenever any one of them says to. Combined, these six adjustments actually made the model's picks noticeably worse, dropping accuracy from about 53.4% to about 50.4% across 1,537 games from 2020-2025, and breaking the combination apart shows two of the six (the injury one and the backup-quarterback one) are doing most of the damage on their own.

overlay_subset_all_seven_joint.plain_summary: This tests combining seven separate experimental adjustments to the model's picks at once -- the same six-adjustment combination covering coaching, injuries, division rematches, backup quarterbacks, playing surface, and spread gaps, plus a seventh flip based on player arrests -- flipping a pick whenever any one of the seven says to. Combining all seven made the model's picks worse still, confirming that stacking more of these adjustments together compounds the damage rather than helping.

overlay_subset_holdout_2020_2022_reverse.plain_summary: This takes one specific combination of three model-pick adjustments (a coach-experience fade, a player-arrests-based flip, and a spread-gap fade) that was chosen because it looked best on the 2023-2025 seasons, and checks whether that same combination still helps when applied to the earlier, untouched 2020-2022 seasons. The limited data leaned toward the combination holding up in the earlier seasons too, though the measured effect there was smaller than the one that led to picking it, as expected whenever a rule is chosen for looking good on one slice of data and then checked on another.

overlay_subset_holdout_2023_2025_frozen.plain_summary: This takes one specific combination of three model-pick adjustments (a coach-experience fade, a division-rematch tilt, and a spread-gap fade) that was chosen because it looked best on the 2020-2022 seasons, and checks whether that same combination still helps when applied to the later, untouched 2023-2025 seasons. The limited data leaned toward the combination holding up in the later seasons too, though again with a smaller measured effect than the one that led to choosing it.

overlay_subset_production_chain_coach_ar.plain_summary: This tests the specific two-adjustment combination the project actually uses in production -- a coach-experience fade plus a player-arrests-based flip -- applied together against the plain model, across 2020-2025 games. The limited data leaned toward this combination being an improvement over the plain model, consistent with why it was adopted, though this check reuses game data the adjustments were already partly built on rather than being a fully fresh test.

overlay_subset_production_plus_division_.plain_summary: This tests adding a third adjustment, a division-rematch tilt, on top of the two the project already uses in production (a coach-experience fade and a player-arrests-based flip), applied together across 2020-2025 games. The limited data leaned toward this being an improvement, but the specific three-way combination was picked by trying many combinations against this same set of games, which tends to inflate how good the winning combination looks.

overlay_subset_production_plus_spread_ga.plain_summary: This tests adding a third adjustment, a fade based on an unusual gap in the point spread, on top of the two the project already uses in production (a coach-experience fade and a player-arrests-based flip), applied together across 2020-2025 games. The limited data leaned toward this being an improvement, but the specific three-way combination was picked by trying many combinations against this same set of games, which tends to inflate how good the winning combination looks.

overlay_subset_reselection_twelve_member.plain_summary: This re-runs the entire process of choosing which combination of model-pick adjustments to play, this time searching all 4,095 possible combinations of twelve candidate adjustments rather than just the four already in use, with the search done only on 2020-2022 games and then checked unchanged on the untouched 2023-2025 games. The freshly re-chosen combination actually did slightly worse on the holdout games than sticking with the four-adjustment combination the project already plays, while blindly combining all twelve adjustments at once did far worse still, and the notes caution that every individual adjustment involved was already built using data this same holdout period overlaps, so even this check isn't a fully clean test.

participation_offense_defense_rapm.plain_summary: This tests adding a more sophisticated measure of which players were on the field for which plays, credited and debited using a technique borrowed from basketball analytics, on top of the model's existing measure of roster value. A separate calibration check shows this project's evaluation tools are simply not sensitive enough to reliably detect an effect this small even if a real one exists, so the inconclusive result reflects the limits of the measuring stick, not necessarily an absence of value.

pbp08_pass_mirror_null.plain_summary: Placebo check for a separate finding about pass-heavy offenses facing weak pass defenses: this repeats the same measurement machinery on a group where both sides are weak by the same definition (bottom-quartile offense against bottom-quartile defense), where nothing in particular should show up. It came back essentially at a coin flip, as a working placebo should.

pbp08_pass_mismatch.plain_summary: An offense that has been unusually effective throwing the ball over its last four games meets a defense that has been unusually poor at defending the pass over the same stretch. Bet on the offense's team; a companion placebo check on similarly weak match-ups, used to confirm the method isn't just inventing noise, came back at a coin flip as it should.

pbp08_protection_mirror_null.plain_summary: Placebo check for a separate finding about a pass-protection mismatch: this repeats the same measurement machinery on a group where both sides are weak by the same definition (an offense that gives up little pressure against a defense that doesn't generate much), where nothing in particular should show up. It came back essentially at a coin flip, as a working placebo should.

pbp08_protection_mismatch.plain_summary: An offense that has been giving up quarterback pressure at a high rate over its last four games meets a defense that has been generating pressure at a high rate over the same stretch. Bet on the defense's team; a companion placebo check on similarly weak match-ups came back at a coin flip, supporting that this isn't just measurement noise.

pbp_drive_bundle.plain_summary: This tests whether a broader bundle of play-by-play and drive-level statistics -- yardage, efficiency, and drive-outcome numbers aggregated beyond what the model already uses -- adds anything on top of the base model, re-checked on a stretch of seasons (2013 to 2017) that hadn't been used to evaluate this particular bundle before. The result came back essentially at a coin flip; part of the uncertainty range attached to this record comes from a script that wasn't independently re-run this session, so it should be treated as unverified until re-checked.

penalty_crew_dpi_tilt_pass_heavy_favorit.plain_summary: The home team is favored, has been a pass-heavy offense lately, and today's officiating crew called defensive pass interference at an unusually high rate last season -- the idea being that a flag-happy crew hands a pass-heavy team extra free yardage and first downs. This was tested as a bet on that home favorite, one of four predeclared officiating-crew-tendency checks, and the limited data leaned against the idea.

penalty_crew_flag_rate_high_total_line.plain_summary: Today's officiating crew calls penalties at an unusually high overall rate, and the game's projected total score is unusually high, a shootout-style matchup -- the idea being that a flag-heavy crew's extra stoppages help the home team, who sets the game plan, control tempo more than the visitor. This was tested as a bet on the home team, one of four predeclared officiating-crew-tendency checks, and the limited data came back close to a coin flip.

penalty_crew_high_flag_heavy_underdog_op.plain_summary: Today's officiating crew calls penalties at an unusually high overall rate, and the home team opened as a big underdog, getting at least seven points -- the idea being that the extra stoppages a flag-heavy crew creates help an overmatched home team control tempo and limit possessions against the better team. This was tested as a bet on that home underdog, graded using the opening betting line, one of four predeclared officiating-crew-tendency checks, and the limited data leaned toward the idea, though the sample of qualifying games is thin enough that this reading is fragile.

penalty_crew_holding_tilt_run_heavy.plain_summary: The home team has been run-heavy lately, and today's officiating crew calls offensive holding at an unusually high rate -- the idea being that extra holding scrutiny disrupts a run-blocking scheme more than a passing one, hurting the home team's ability to sustain drives. This was tested as a bet against that home team, one of four predeclared officiating-crew-tendency checks, and the limited data actually leaned the other way, toward the home team covering more often in this situation, not less.

penalty_discipline.plain_summary: A team has been among the least penalized in the league over the prior season, compared with the most penalized, checked as a factor in whether that cleaner team covers the spread more often. The limited data leaned toward cleaner teams covering slightly more often, but the underlying numbers here had to be rebuilt from scratch after the original calculation script was lost, so this figure carries extra uncertainty about exactly matching the original measurement.

pick_conditioned_off_bye_fade_pre2018.plain_summary: Among games where the prediction model's own pick is the team coming off a bye week with much more rest than its opponent, an earlier look at 2018-2025 games found those particular picks landing right only about 41% to 44% of the time -- worse than the rest of the slate. This entry re-tests that same warning sign on the 2011-2017 seasons, and the limited data leaned away from the warning sign repeating in that older era.

pick_conditioned_rest_mismatch_pre2018.plain_summary: Among games where the prediction model's own pick involves two teams with unequal days of rest between them, an earlier look at 2018-2025 games found those picks landing right less often than picks in games where both teams had the same rest. This entry re-tests that same warning sign on the 2011-2017 seasons, and the limited data leaned toward the warning sign holding up in that older era too.

pick_conditioned_road_favorite_pre2018.plain_summary: Among games where the prediction model's own pick is a team favored by the betting market despite playing on the road, an earlier look at 2018-2025 games found those picks landing right noticeably more often than the rest of the slate. This entry re-tests that same encouraging sign on the 2011-2017 seasons, and the limited data came back close to even, neither confirming nor overturning it.

pick_conditioned_spread_gap_zone_pre2018.plain_summary: Among games where the point spread sits between roughly a touchdown and ten points, an earlier look at 2018-2025 games found the prediction model's own picks in that particular spread range landing right less often than the rest of the slate. This entry re-tests that same warning sign on the 2011-2017 seasons, and the limited data leaned strongly toward the warning sign holding up in that older era too.

player_arrests_recent_14d_back_side_poli.plain_summary: This tests a specific policy: whenever the model's own weekly pick goes against a team that had a player named in a news report about a police incident within the last two weeks, flip the pick to back that team instead. Tested against the model's original picks at the opening line, the limited data leaned toward this flip-the-pick policy helping accuracy, though it is not adopted.

player_arrests_recent_14d_fade_close.plain_summary: A team had a player named in a news report about a police incident within the last two weeks. This was tested as a bet against that team, graded against the closing line, and the limited data leaned strongly away from the idea working.

player_arrests_recent_14d_fade_opener.plain_summary: A team had a player named in a news report about a police incident within the last two weeks. This was tested as a bet against that team, graded against the opening line, and the limited data leaned away from the idea working, though the secondary season-by-season check behind this number used too few time blocks to be trustworthy on its own.

player_arrests_violent_person_recent_14d.plain_summary: A team had a player named in a more serious, violence-related police-incident report within the last two weeks. This was tested as a bet against that team, graded against the closing line, and the limited data came back almost exactly a coin flip.

A team had a player named in a more serious, violence-related police-incident report within the last two weeks. This was tested as a bet against that team, graded against the opening line, and the limited data leaned away from the idea working, though the secondary season-by-season check behind this number used too few time blocks to be trustworthy on its own.

player_family_base_vs_continuity.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game: this tests whether adding information about how stable each team's starting lineup has been to the prediction model, on top of a bare-bones baseline using only market and game-context information, improves accuracy over the 2018-2025 seasons. The limited data leaned toward this feature block helping, but it is one of eight overlapping feature comparisons sharing the same 2,075 games with each other, so it should not be treated as independent evidence.

player_family_base_vs_injuries.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game: this tests whether adding a straightforward count of each team's injured players to the prediction model, on top of a bare-bones baseline using only market and game-context information, improves accuracy over the 2018-2025 seasons. The limited data leaned slightly toward this feature block helping, but it is one of eight overlapping feature comparisons sharing the same 2,075 games with each other, so it should not be treated as independent evidence.

player_family_base_vs_injuries_continuit.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game: this tests whether adding both an injury count and a lineup-stability measure together to the prediction model, on top of a bare-bones baseline using only market and game-context information, improves accuracy over the 2018-2025 seasons. The limited data leaned toward this combined feature block helping, but it is one of eight overlapping feature comparisons sharing the same 2,075 games with each other, so it should not be treated as independent evidence.

player_family_base_vs_injury_value.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game: this tests whether adding a measure of how valuable the specific injured players are, not just how many are hurt, to the prediction model on top of a bare-bones baseline using only market and game-context information, improves accuracy over the 2018-2025 seasons. The limited data leaned toward this feature block helping, but it is one of eight overlapping feature comparisons sharing the same 2,075 games with each other, so it should not be treated as independent evidence.

player_family_base_vs_qb.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game: this tests whether adding quarterback-specific features to the prediction model, on top of a bare-bones baseline using only market and game-context information, improves accuracy over the 2018-2025 seasons. The limited data leaned away from this feature block helping, but it is one of eight overlapping feature comparisons sharing the same 2,075 games with each other, so it should not be treated as independent evidence.

player_family_base_vs_qb_continuity.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game: this tests whether adding quarterback-specific features together with a lineup-stability measure to the prediction model, on top of a bare-bones baseline using only market and game-context information, improves accuracy over the 2018-2025 seasons. The limited data leaned strongly toward this combined feature block helping, the strongest lean of this whole feature-comparison group, but it is one of eight overlapping comparisons sharing the same 2,075 games with each other, so it should not be treated as independent evidence. A different pair of entries elsewhere in this registry tests a related quarterback-plus-continuity comparison on an earlier set of seasons with a different baseline.

player_family_base_vs_qb_injuries.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game: this tests whether adding quarterback-specific features together with an injury count to the prediction model, on top of a bare-bones baseline using only market and game-context information, improves accuracy over the 2018-2025 seasons. The limited data leaned away from this combined feature block helping, but it is one of eight overlapping feature comparisons sharing the same 2,075 games with each other, so it should not be treated as independent evidence.

player_family_base_vs_value.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game: this tests whether adding a measure of the total on-field value lost to injuries to the prediction model, on top of a bare-bones baseline using only market and game-context information, improves accuracy over the 2018-2025 seasons. The limited data leaned toward this feature block helping, but it is one of eight overlapping feature comparisons sharing the same 2,075 games with each other, so it should not be treated as independent evidence.

player_qb_continuity_bundled_alpha.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game: this is an old, since-superseded comparison of adding quarterback-and-lineup-continuity features to the model that changed two things in the model at once, both the feature set and a smoothing setting called regularization, making it impossible to tell which change did what. A cleaner comparison elsewhere in this registry changes only the feature set while holding the smoothing setting fixed; this bundled entry adds no new information on its own and is stored here at zero effect for record-keeping only.

player_qb_continuity_matched_alpha.plain_summary: Not a bet on any single game: this tests whether adding quarterback-and-lineup-continuity features to the model helps, with the model's smoothing setting held fixed so only the feature set differs between the two versions being compared, on 997 games from the 2014-2017 seasons. The limited data leaned toward the feature block helping; a later re-check found an earlier version of this comparison had used too few time blocks to trust, and the corrected version, on the same games, points the same direction and is now better supported.

proxy_opener_production_rule_2009_2019.plain_summary: This is an instrument check, not a bet on any game: it estimates how well the prediction model would have performed in the 2011-2019 seasons, for which the project doesn't have real archived opening-line data, by substituting a very similar opening line pulled from a different odds archive as a stand-in. Using that stand-in, the model's accuracy in those older seasons came out around 50.4%, noticeably closer to a coin flip than the roughly 53% to 54% the model achieves in recent seasons with the real opening line, and a companion check on overlapping seasons found only a small, inconclusive part of that gap is explained by the stand-in line differing from the real one -- the rest of the difference is unexplained.

pt_away_underdog.plain_summary: The visiting team is an underdog playing in a nationally-televised primetime game (Thursday or Monday night, or a Sunday night kickoff at 8pm ET or later). This was tested as a bet on that team, on the idea that bettors overreact to the spotlight and inflate the price on the home favorite, and the limited data leaned away from the idea.

pt_divisional_favorite.plain_summary: A team is favored by the betting market in a primetime game against a division rival, a hostile road environment thought to compress final margins. This was tested as a bet against that favorite, and the limited data came back essentially a coin flip.

pt_off_loss.plain_summary: A team is playing in a primetime game immediately after losing its previous game, a spot where teams are thought to respond with a stronger effort. This was tested as a bet on that team, and the limited data came back essentially a coin flip.

pt_off_win.plain_summary: A team is playing in a primetime game immediately after winning its previous game, included mainly as a comparison point with no strong reason to expect an edge either way. This was tested as a bet on that team, and the limited data came back essentially a coin flip, leaning only very slightly positive.

pt_post_mnf_sunday.plain_summary: A team is playing on Sunday just six days after playing its own game on Monday night, a short-turnaround spot with less recovery time than usual. This was tested as a bet against that team, and the limited data leaned toward the bet working, though the effect turned out to be driven entirely by the earlier years in the sample and did not hold up in more recent seasons.

pt_post_mnf_sunday_era_2009_2017.plain_summary: A team is playing on Sunday just six days after playing its own game on Monday night, a short-turnaround spot with less recovery time than usual, checked only in the 2009 through 2017 seasons. This was tested as a bet against that team, and the limited data from that era leaned strongly toward the bet working.

pt_post_mnf_sunday_era_2018_2025.plain_summary: A team is playing on Sunday just six days after playing its own game on Monday night, a short-turnaround spot with less recovery time than usual, checked only in the 2018 through 2025 seasons. This was tested as a bet against that team, and in this more recent era the data leaned the opposite way, undercutting the case that the short-turnaround effect is real and stable.

public_betting_battery_fade_heavy_public.plain_summary: The betting public has piled at least 70% of their bets onto one side of the game. This was tested as a bet against that heavily-backed side, graded against the closing line, using an archive that only covers about a third of games in a typical season, and the limited data leaned strongly away from the idea working.

The betting public has piled at least 70% of their bets onto one side of the game. This was tested as a bet against that heavily-backed side, graded against the opening line, using an archive with sparse coverage of games, and the limited data leaned away from the idea working.

public_betting_battery_model_interaction.plain_summary: This checks how accurate the prediction model's own picks are specifically in games where the betting public has piled heavily, 70% or more of bets, onto the side the model did NOT choose. Graded against the closing line using an archive with sparse coverage of games, the limited data leaned away from the model doing especially well in that spot.

This compares how accurate the prediction model's own picks are when the betting public is heavily piled against the model's chosen side versus when the public is heavily piled with it. On a small sample of roughly 90 games split between the two situations, the limited data leaned toward the model doing worse when it disagrees with a heavily-backed public side, though the sample is small and the result is inconclusive.

public_betting_battery_sharp_divergence_.plain_summary: The share of total money wagered on one side of the game is at least 15 percentage points higher than the share of individual bets placed on that side, a gap that can signal larger, more informed bettors are concentrated there. This was tested as a bet on that side, graded against the closing line, on a later portion of the betting-data archive where this money-versus-bets breakdown is available, and the limited data leaned away from the idea working.

qb_age_rookie_late_improvement.plain_summary: A team is starting a quarterback with six or fewer career starts, in week 9 or later of the season, on the idea that first-year starters improve as the season goes on. This was tested as a bet on that team, and the limited data leaned against the idea, though it stayed just short of ruling it out.

qb_age_rookie_vs_pressure.plain_summary: A team is starting a quarterback with six or fewer career starts against a defense that was among the league's best last season at pressuring the quarterback, measured with a stand-in for blitz rate since that exact stat wasn't available. This was tested as a bet against that inexperienced-quarterback team, and the limited data leaned away from the idea.

qb_age_second_year_jump.plain_summary: A team is starting a quarterback in their second year as a starter, after making their first career start the previous season, on the idea that quarterbacks often take a step forward in year two. This was tested as a bet on that team, and the limited data leaned strongly toward the idea, the strongest lean among a related group of quarterback-experience checks.

qb_age_veteran_late_fade.plain_summary: A team is starting a quarterback with 200 or more career starts, late in the season (week 13 or beyond), on the idea that very experienced quarterbacks fade down the stretch. This was tested as a bet against that team, but only 94 games qualified, far too few to say anything meaningful, and the limited data leaned away from the idea.

qb_news_backup_visible_by_deadline_scree.plain_summary: A team is starting a backup quarterback, restricted to the cases where sports-news outlets had already reported the backup would likely start before the pick deadline, rather than it coming as a surprise. Teams starting a backup quarterback generally cover less often overall, but this narrower slice, where the change was foreshadowed in the news, leaned the same losing direction only weakly, suggesting the betting market may already price in backup-quarterback news reported in advance, unlike a truly surprise change; that explanation is inferred here, not directly proven.

recurrence_flags_player_brier_validation.plain_summary: Not a bet on games directly: this measures whether tracking a player's history of repeat injuries to the same body part improves the model's forecast of whether that player will be available for next week's game, scored on a probability-accuracy scale (Brier score) rather than the usual pick-accuracy percentage, using 2022 data to build the method and 2023 games held out to check it. This entry had two bookkeeping errors caught and fixed in the same update, a wrong interval paired with the number and a flipped plus/minus sign; corrected, the recurrence-history information only beats an already-outdated, uncalibrated baseline, and the apparent gain disappears once that baseline is properly calibrated.

reddit_away_comment_ratio_elevated.plain_summary: The visiting team's fan subreddit is unusually argumentative that week, getting far more comments per post than that team's own normal pattern, a proxy for fan anxiety or controversy. This was tested as a bet on the home team, one of several similar Reddit-based comparisons tried together as a batch, and the limited data leaned toward the idea.

reddit_away_spike_value.plain_summary: The visiting team's fan subreddit is seeing an unusual spike in overall posting and commenting activity that week compared with that team's own normal pattern. This was tested as a bet on the home team, one of several similar Reddit-based comparisons tried together as a batch, and the limited data leaned toward the idea.

reddit_home_comment_ratio_elevated.plain_summary: The home team's fan subreddit is unusually argumentative that week, getting far more comments per post than that team's own normal pattern, a proxy for fan anxiety or controversy. This was tested as a bet against that home team, one of several similar Reddit-based comparisons tried together as a batch, and the limited data leaned strongly toward the idea.

reddit_home_spike_fade.plain_summary: The home team's fan subreddit is seeing an unusual spike in overall posting and commenting activity that week compared with that team's own normal pattern. This was tested as a bet against that home team, one of several similar Reddit-based comparisons tried together as a batch, and the limited data leaned away from the idea.

reddit_spike_gap_home_worse.plain_summary: Only the home team's fan subreddit is seeing an unusual activity spike that week while the visiting team's subreddit is not (or vice versa), comparing games where just one side's fans are unusually loud. This was tested as a bet against the home team specifically when it's their own fans who spiked, one of several similar Reddit-based comparisons tried together as a batch, and the limited data leaned away from the idea on a small sample of qualifying games.

redteam_body_clock_night_increment_withi.plain_summary: This is a stress-test of the West Coast body-clock travel effect: among West Coast teams playing a road game at night (8pm ET kickoff or later), it isolates the effect of the late kickoff time itself while holding travel distance constant. It leaned toward hurting those teams' covering rate, but the notes are explicit that this check alone cannot cleanly separate how much of the effect is the late kickoff versus the travel distance, and it should not be treated as independent evidence alongside the related body-clock entries it decomposes.

redteam_body_clock_night_west_road_dista.plain_summary: This is a follow-up check on the West Coast body-clock travel effect: it asks whether a West Coast team's road game at night really comes down to sheer travel distance, by testing for an effect specifically tied to being a West Coast team even after accounting for how far it traveled. The answer leaned clearly toward no, the effect held up even after controlling for distance, but this uses a quicker statistical shortcut than the project's usual method and is explicitly flagged as not independent evidence from the related body-clock entries it decomposes.
